---- MODULE W4Od2m9p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bots, Zones, MaxLimit, MaxEpoch, NoZone

VARIABLES layout, ceiling, permit, issued

vars == <<layout, ceiling, permit, issued>>

Current(r) == permit[r] # NoZone /\ issued[r] = layout
Inside(z) == {r \in Bots : permit[r] = z /\ issued[r] = layout}
Stale(r) == permit[r] # NoZone /\ issued[r] # layout

TypeOK ==
    /\ layout \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ ceiling \in [Zones -> 1 .. MaxLimit]
    /\ permit \in [Bots -> Zones \cup {NoZone}]
    /\ issued \in [Bots -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ layout = 0
    /\ ceiling = [z \in Zones |-> MaxLimit]
    /\ permit = [r \in Bots |-> NoZone]
    /\ issued = [r \in Bots |-> 0]

\* A permit is stamped with the layout epoch it was issued under, and only
\* permits stamped with the running epoch count towards a zone's ceiling.
Admit(r, z) ==
    /\ permit[r] = NoZone
    /\ Cardinality(Inside(z)) < ceiling[z]
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = z]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![r] = layout]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling>>

Exit(r) ==
    /\ permit[r] # NoZone
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = NoZone]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling, issued>>

\* Renewing re-checks the ceiling under the running epoch, so a bot cannot
\* carry an old permit into a zone that has since been tightened.
Renew(r) ==
    /\ Stale(r)
    /\ Cardinality(Inside(permit[r])) < ceiling[permit[r]]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![r] = layout]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling, permit>>

\* Reconfiguration retimes the floor: ceilings are rewritten and the layout
\* epoch advances, which puts every permit issued earlier behind.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ layout < MaxEpoch
    /\ ceiling' = c
    /\ layout' = layout + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, issued>>

\* The floor controller sweeps every behind-the-epoch permit in one pass.
Purge ==
    /\ \E r \in Bots : Stale(r)
    /\ permit' = [r \in Bots |-> IF Stale(r) THEN NoZone ELSE permit[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling, issued>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Bots, z \in Zones : Admit(r, z)
    \/ \E r \in Bots : Exit(r) \/ Renew(r)
    \/ \E c \in [Zones -> 1 .. MaxLimit] : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ Purge

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Purge)

\* No zone ever holds more bots on current permits than its ceiling allows.
ZoneCeilingHolds ==
    \A z \in Zones : Cardinality(Inside(z)) <= ceiling[z]

\* Permits left behind by a reconfiguration do not linger.
StalePermitsClear ==
    (\E r \in Bots : Stale(r)) ~> (\A r \in Bots : ~Stale(r))

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bots = {btPick, btPack}
    Zones = {znAisle, znDock}
    MaxLimit = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoZone = NoZone
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ZoneCeilingHolds
PROPERTY StalePermitsClear
nl:
A warehouse floor is divided into zones, and each zone has a ceiling on how many robots may be
inside it at once. The ceiling is a safety limit — too many machines in one aisle and they deadlock
against each other and block the pickers — so it must never be exceeded.

The floor plan is numbered by epoch. A robot is admitted to a zone by being issued a permit, and the
permit is stamped with the layout epoch that was running when it was issued. Only permits stamped
with the running epoch count towards a zone's ceiling: a permit from an earlier epoch describes a
floor that no longer exists and carries no weight at all. A robot leaves a zone by giving up its
permit. A robot whose permit is behind can renew it against the running epoch, but renewing
re-checks the ceiling, so it cannot walk an old permit into a zone that has since been tightened.

Capacity changes while the fleet is working. Reconfiguration rewrites the ceilings — the dock is
widened for a container, the aisle is narrowed for a pallet drop — and rolls the layout epoch on,
wrapping at the top of its range. Every permit issued before the change is behind from that moment.
The floor controller sweeps behind-the-epoch permits away in a single pass, and permits left behind
by a reconfiguration never linger indefinitely.

The full set of actions is: Admit, in which a robot with no permit is let into a zone whose current
permits are below its ceiling, and the permit is stamped with the running epoch; Exit, in which a
robot gives up its permit; Renew, in which a robot holding a behind-the-epoch permit brings it up to
the running epoch, subject to the zone's ceiling; Reconfigure, in which the ceilings are rewritten
and the layout epoch advances; and Purge, in which the floor controller clears every
behind-the-epoch permit in one pass.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No zone ever holds more robots on current-epoch permits than that zone's ceiling
allows.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Permits left behind by a reconfiguration are eventually all cleared, so the floor
never carries stale permits for ever.

---- MODULE W4Od15m6p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Engines, Books, Horizon, MaxWindow, Vacant, NoBook

VARIABLES grant, clock, actedAt, actedOn

vars == <<grant, clock, actedAt, actedOn>>

Windows == [book: Books, from: 0 .. Horizon, until: 1 .. Horizon]

LiveOn(k, e) ==
    /\ grant[e] # Vacant
    /\ grant[e].book = k
    /\ grant[e].until >= clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ grant \in [Engines -> Windows \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ actedAt \in [Engines -> 0 .. Horizon]
    /\ actedOn \in [Engines -> Books \cup {NoBook}]

Init ==
    /\ grant = [e \in Engines |-> Vacant]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ actedAt = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ actedOn = [e \in Engines |-> NoBook]

\* The two venues share one pool of books, so a window is only let on a book
\* no other venue currently holds a live window on.
Take(e, k, len) ==
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ \A f \in Engines : f # e => ~LiveOn(k, f)
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![e] = [book |-> k, from |-> clock, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ actedAt' = [actedAt EXCEPT ![e] = 0]
    /\ actedOn' = [actedOn EXCEPT ![e] = NoBook]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* A venue may only match into a book inside the window it was let, and the
\* match is stamped with the time it happened.
Match(e) ==
    /\ grant[e] # Vacant
    /\ clock >= grant[e].from
    /\ clock <= grant[e].until
    /\ actedAt' = [actedAt EXCEPT ![e] = clock]
    /\ actedOn' = [actedOn EXCEPT ![e] = grant[e].book]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, actedAt, actedOn>>

\* Windows are not torn up when they run out; they stay on the record so the
\* auditor can check every match against the window it was made under.
Surrender(e) ==
    /\ grant[e] # Vacant
    /\ grant[e].until < clock
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![e] = Vacant]
    /\ actedOn' = [actedOn EXCEPT ![e] = NoBook]
    /\ actedAt' = [actedAt EXCEPT ![e] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Reopen ==
    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ grant' = [e \in Engines |-> Vacant]
    /\ actedAt' = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ actedOn' = [e \in Engines |-> NoBook]

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines, k \in Books, n \in 1 .. MaxWindow : Take(e, k, n)
    \/ \E e \in Engines : Match(e) \/ Surrender(e)
    \/ Tick \/ Reopen

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every match on the record was made into the book the venue held a window
\* on, at a time inside that window -- never early, never after it ran out.
ActsWithinWindow ==
    \A e \in Engines :
        actedOn[e] # NoBook =>
            /\ grant[e] # Vacant
            /\ grant[e].book = actedOn[e]
            /\ grant[e].from <= actedAt[e]
            /\ actedAt[e] <= grant[e].until

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Engines = {enPrimary, enBackup}
    Books = {bkEquity, bkBond}
    Horizon = 2
    MaxWindow = 2
    Vacant = Vacant
    NoBook = NoBook
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ActsWithinWindow
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction on two matching venues that were built and certified
separately — a primary and a backup — and both of them can reach the same pool of order books. The
regulator's concern is participation: a venue must only match into a book it has actually been given
the right to, and only during the period it was given, so that every match on the record can be tied
back to a live entitlement.

The right to match is let as a window: a book, a start time and an end time. A venue is let a window
on a book only if no other venue currently holds a live window on that same book, and only if the
end time falls inside the auction horizon. Taking a new window wipes whatever the venue had recorded
before, because the old entitlement no longer describes what it is doing.

A venue matches into the book named on its window, and only while the clock is at or after the
window's start and at or before its end. Every match is stamped with the time it happened and the
book it went into. Windows are deliberately not torn up the moment they run out: they stay on the
record so that the auditor can check each venue's last match against the window it was made under. A
venue can surrender a window that has run out, and doing so clears its record along with it. At the
end of the horizon the auction is reopened: the clock goes back to the start and every window and
record is cleared.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a venue is let a window on a book no other venue holds a
live window on, ending inside the horizon, and its record is wiped; Match, in which a venue matches
into the book on its window while the clock is inside that window, stamping the time and the book;
Tick, in which the auction clock advances; Surrender, in which a venue gives up a window that has
run out and clears its record; and Reopen, in which the clock is reset and every window and record
is cleared.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every match on the record was made into the book named on the venue's window, at a
time at or after that window opened and at or before it ran out, so no venue is ever recorded acting
outside a live entitlement.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m4p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Groups, Tags, Stock, QCap

VARIABLES fridge, bench, van, wards

vars == <<fridge, bench, van, wards>>

Consignments == [tag: Tags, grp: Groups]

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridge \in 0 .. Stock
    /\ Len(bench) <= QCap
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(bench) : bench[i] \in Groups
    /\ van \subseteq Consignments
    /\ wards \in 0 .. Stock

Init ==
    /\ fridge = Stock
    /\ bench = <<>>
    /\ van = {}
    /\ wards = 0

\* Backpressure: nothing else is cross-matched once the bench is full.
Crossmatch(g) ==
    /\ fridge > 0
    /\ Len(bench) < QCap
    /\ fridge' = fridge - 1
    /\ bench' = Append(bench, g)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<van, wards>>

\* Consignments are tagged so two otherwise identical units stay distinct on
\* the van; the tag is reused only once nothing bearing it is out.
Load(t) ==
    /\ bench # <<>>
    /\ \A m \in van : m.tag # t
    /\ van' = van \cup {[tag |-> t, grp |-> Head(bench)]}
    /\ bench' = Tail(bench)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, wards>>

\* The van is not a queue: consignments are signed for in whatever order the
\* wards get to them.
Sign(m) ==
    /\ m \in van
    /\ van' = van \ {m}
    /\ wards' = wards + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, bench>>

Divert(m) ==
    /\ m \in van
    /\ van' = van \ {m}
    /\ fridge' = fridge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bench, wards>>

\* The round always ends back at the bank: whatever is still on the van when
\* the driver books off is signed in to the wards it was routed to.
CloseRound ==
    /\ van # {}
    /\ wards' = wards + Cardinality(van)
    /\ van' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, bench>>

Return ==
    /\ wards > 0
    /\ wards' = wards - 1
    /\ fridge' = fridge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bench, van>>

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Groups : Crossmatch(g)
    \/ \E t \in Tags : Load(t)
    \/ \E m \in van : Sign(m) \/ Divert(m)
    \/ CloseRound \/ Return

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(CloseRound)

\* Every unit in the bank is in exactly one place -- fridge, cross-match bench,
\* van or ward -- so the four counts always add up to the bank's stock.
UnitsConserved ==
    fridge + Len(bench) + Cardinality(van) + wards = Stock

\* The van never stays loaded: every round is closed out.
VanClears == (van # {}) ~> (van = {})

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Groups = {gOneg, gABpos}
    Tags = {tgA, tgB}
    Stock = 3
    QCap = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT UnitsConserved
PROPERTY VanClears
nl:
A hospital blood bank tracks every unit it holds. A unit is always in exactly one place — in the
cold store, on the cross-match bench waiting to go out, on the delivery van, or up on a ward — and
the tracker's whole job is that the four counts always add up to the bank's stock. A unit that
appears in two places at once, or in none, is a unit somebody is about to transfuse twice or not at
all.

Units leave the cold store onto the cross-match bench, which is bounded and applies backpressure:
once the bench is at its cap nothing further is cross-matched and the units stay in the store. The
bench is worked from the front — the unit that has been waiting longest is the next one loaded onto
the van.

Consignments on the van carry tags so that two units of the same group stay distinct, and a tag is
reused only when nothing bearing it is still out. The van is not a queue: it does its rounds and
consignments are signed for by the wards in whatever order the wards get to them, so a unit loaded
first may well be signed for last. A consignment can also be diverted back to the cold store instead
of being delivered.

The round always ends back at the bank. When the driver books off, whatever is still on the van is
signed in to the wards it was routed to, so the van never stays loaded. Units that a ward does not
use come back into the cold store.

The full set of actions is: Crossmatch, in which a unit leaves the cold store for the tail of the
bench while the bench is below its cap; Load, in which the unit at the front of the bench goes onto
the van under a free tag; Sign, in which any consignment on the van, in any order, is signed for by
a ward; Divert, in which any consignment on the van goes back into the cold store; CloseRound, in
which the driver books off and everything still on the van is signed in to the wards; and Return, in
which a unit comes back from a ward into the cold store.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units in the cold store, on the cross-match bench, on the van and up on the
wards always add up to exactly the bank's stock.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The van never stays loaded — whenever consignments are out, the round is
eventually closed out and the van is empty.

---- MODULE W4Od15m2p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Slots, Parties, NoProp

VARIABLES prop, ballot, allocs, withdrawn

vars == <<prop, ballot, allocs, withdrawn>>

Allocations == [slot: Slots, desk: Desks]

Taken(s) == \E a \in allocs : a.slot = s

TypeOK ==
    /\ prop \in [Desks -> Slots \cup {NoProp}]
    /\ ballot \in [Desks -> [Parties -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
    /\ allocs \subseteq Allocations
    /\ withdrawn \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ prop = [d \in Desks |-> NoProp]
    /\ ballot = [d \in Desks |-> [p \in Parties |-> "none"]]
    /\ allocs = {}
    /\ withdrawn = {}

\* Both desks draw opening slots from the same pool and are free to prepare
\* the same slot at the same time; the commit check is what separates them.
Prepare(d, s) ==
    /\ prop[d] = NoProp
    /\ s \notin withdrawn
    /\ ~Taken(s)
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![d] = s]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![d] = [p \in Parties |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, withdrawn>>

Aye(d, p) ==
    /\ prop[d] # NoProp
    /\ ballot[d][p] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![d][p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, allocs, withdrawn>>

Nay(d, p) ==
    /\ prop[d] # NoProp
    /\ ballot[d][p] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![d][p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, allocs, withdrawn>>

\* The slot is re-checked at commit time, not just at prepare time: a slot
\* taken while the ballot was running takes the round down with it.
Commit(d) ==
    /\ prop[d] # NoProp
    /\ \A p \in Parties : ballot[d][p] = "yes"
    /\ ~Taken(prop[d])
    /\ prop[d] \notin withdrawn
    /\ allocs' = allocs \cup {[slot |-> prop[d], desk |-> d]}
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![d] = NoProp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, withdrawn>>

Abort(d) ==
    /\ prop[d] # NoProp
    /\ \/ \E p \in Parties : ballot[d][p] = "no"
       \/ Taken(prop[d])
       \/ prop[d] \in withdrawn
    /\ prop' = [prop EXCEPT ![d] = NoProp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, allocs, withdrawn>>

Hand(a) ==
    /\ a \in allocs
    /\ allocs' = allocs \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, ballot, withdrawn>>

Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ s \notin withdrawn
    /\ ~Taken(s)
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, ballot, allocs>>

Reoffer(s) ==
    /\ s \in withdrawn
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prop, ballot, allocs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots : Prepare(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, p \in Parties : Aye(d, p) \/ Nay(d, p)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Commit(d) \/ Abort(d)
    \/ \E a \in allocs : Hand(a)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Withdraw(s) \/ Reoffer(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The allocation register is a function of the slot: two allocations for the
\* same opening slot can only be the same allocation, so no slot is ever
\* handed to both desks.
SlotAllocatedOnce ==
    \A a, b \in allocs : a.slot = b.slot => a.desk = b.desk

====
nl:
A stock exchange sells opening auction slots — the matching windows in which a security's opening
price is struck. Two trading desks, cash and derivatives, run their own scheduling systems and were
never wired together, but both draw slots from the same pool. A slot goes to one desk and one desk
only: two desks holding the same opening window means two opening prices struck for one security.

Each allocation is agreed by two-phase commit across the parties that have to sign it off, the
clearing house and the registrar. A desk prepares a slot that is neither already allocated nor
withdrawn from the pool, which opens a ballot. Each party casts one vote on that desk's ballot. Both
desks can have a ballot running at once, and nothing stops them from running ballots on the same
slot — the desks cannot see each other.

That is why the slot is re-checked at commit time rather than only at prepare time. A ballot commits
only if every party voted in favour and the slot is still free and still on offer at that moment; the
allocation is then written into the register. If a party voted against, or the slot was taken or
withdrawn while the ballot was running, the round aborts with nothing written. Allocations are handed
back when the auction for that slot is done.

Slots can also be withdrawn from the pool while unallocated — a security is suspended, a listing is
pulled — and put back on offer later.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a desk with no ballot running opens one on a slot that
is free and on offer; Aye and Nay, in which a party casts its single vote on a desk's ballot;
Commit, in which a unanimous ballot whose slot is still free and still on offer writes the
allocation into the register; Abort, in which a vote against, or the slot being taken or withdrawn,
ends the round with nothing written; Hand, in which an allocation is given back; Withdraw, in which
an unallocated slot is pulled from the pool; and Reoffer, in which a withdrawn slot goes back on
offer.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The allocation register is a function of the slot — any two entries for the same
opening slot name the same desk — so a slot is never allocated to both desks.

---- MODULE W4Od5m3p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Shards, Nodes, MaxTerm, MaxRev, NoChief, NoEdit

VARIABLES roster, pending, chief, term, cached

vars == <<roster, pending, chief, term, cached>>

Edits == [by: Shards, base: 0 .. MaxRev]
Pends == [by: Shards, base: 0 .. MaxRev, term: 0 .. MaxTerm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ Len(roster) <= MaxRev
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(roster) : roster[i] \in Edits
    /\ pending \in Pends \cup {NoEdit}
    /\ chief \in [Shards -> Nodes \cup {NoChief}]
    /\ term \in [Shards -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ cached \in [Shards -> 0 .. MaxRev]

Init ==
    /\ roster = <<>>
    /\ pending = NoEdit
    /\ chief = [s \in Shards |-> NoChief]
    /\ term = [s \in Shards |-> 0]
    /\ cached = [s \in Shards |-> 0]

Elect(s, n) ==
    /\ chief[s] = NoChief
    /\ term[s] < MaxTerm
    /\ chief' = [chief EXCEPT ![s] = n]
    /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, pending, cached>>

Fail(s) ==
    /\ chief[s] # NoChief
    /\ chief' = [chief EXCEPT ![s] = NoChief]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, pending, term, cached>>

Refetch(s) ==
    /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![s] = Len(roster)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, pending, chief, term>>

\* A shard's chief proposes an edit built on the revision that shard last read,
\* stamped with the leadership it was prepared under.
Propose(s) ==
    /\ pending = NoEdit
    /\ chief[s] # NoChief
    /\ pending' = [by |-> s, base |-> cached[s], term |-> term[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, chief, term, cached>>

\* The edit lands only if it was built on the newest revision and the
\* leadership that prepared it is still the leadership in place.
Apply ==
    /\ pending # NoEdit
    /\ chief[pending.by] # NoChief
    /\ pending.term = term[pending.by]
    /\ pending.base = Len(roster)
    /\ Len(roster) < MaxRev
    /\ roster' = Append(roster, [by |-> pending.by, base |-> pending.base])
    /\ pending' = NoEdit
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, term, cached>>

Refuse ==
    /\ pending # NoEdit
    /\ \/ chief[pending.by] = NoChief
       \/ pending.term # term[pending.by]
       \/ pending.base # Len(roster)
       \/ Len(roster) = MaxRev
    /\ pending' = NoEdit
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, chief, term, cached>>

Archive ==
    /\ pending = NoEdit
    /\ Len(roster) = MaxRev
    /\ roster' = <<>>
    /\ cached' = [s \in Shards |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, chief, term>>

Resolving == Apply \/ Refuse

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Shards, n \in Nodes : Elect(s, n)
    \/ \E s \in Shards : Fail(s) \/ Refetch(s) \/ Propose(s)
    \/ Resolving \/ Archive

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Resolving)

\* Every edit in the party roster was built on the revision immediately before
\* it, so no shard's write was ever laid down over one it had not read.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A i \in 1 .. Len(roster) : roster[i].base = i - 1

\* The registry never sits on a proposal: each one is landed or refused.
ProposalsResolve == (pending # NoEdit) ~> (pending = NoEdit)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Shards = {shWest, shEast}
    Nodes = {ndOne, ndTwo}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxRev = 3
    NoChief = NoChief
    NoEdit = NoEdit
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY ProposalsResolve
nl:
A multiplayer game's matchmaker runs as two independently deployed shards, west and east, that both
write to the same shared party roster. The roster is versioned: revision one is the first edit ever
landed, revision two the next, and so on. The hazard is a lost update — one shard laying its edit
down over a revision it never read, quietly wiping what the other shard just wrote.

Each shard runs its own leader election with failover. A shard with no chief elects one, and the
election advances that shard's leadership term. A chief can fail at any moment, leaving its shard
without one until the next election. Only a shard that currently has a chief prepares edits.

A shard keeps a cached copy of the roster's revision number and refetches it from the registry when
it wants to. When its chief prepares an edit, the edit is stamped both with the revision the shard
last read and with the leadership term it was prepared under. The registry holds one proposal at a
time and never sits on it.

The registry lands an edit only if two things still hold: the edit was built on the newest revision
in the roster, and the leadership that prepared it is still the leadership in place on that shard. An
edit built on a revision that has since been superseded is refused, and so is one prepared under a
chief that has since failed and been replaced. A refused edit changes nothing and the shard starts
again. When the roster reaches the end of its revision range it is archived and the shards' cached
revisions go back to zero.

The full set of actions is: Elect, in which a shard with no chief elects one and advances its term;
Fail, in which a shard's chief drops out; Refetch, in which a shard reads the roster's current
revision into its cache; Propose, in which a shard's chief lodges an edit stamped with its cached
revision and its term; Apply, in which the registry lands an edit built on the newest revision under
the leadership still in place; Refuse, in which the registry turns an edit down because the revision
moved, the leadership changed, the shard has no chief or the roster is full; and Archive, in which a
full roster is cleared and the cached revisions are reset.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every edit in the party roster was built on the revision immediately preceding it,
so no shard's write was ever laid down over a revision it had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal lodged with the registry is eventually either landed or refused.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Segments, Slots, Tracks, NoOne

Books == Segments \X Slots
SegOf(b) == b[1]

VARIABLES seg, latch, resting, slow

vars == <<seg, latch, resting, slow>>

Hands == Members \cup {NoOne}
Latched == {b \in Books : latch[b] # NoOne}

TypeOK ==
    /\ seg \in [Segments -> Hands]
    /\ latch \in [Books -> Hands]
    /\ resting \in [Books -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ slow \subseteq Members

Init ==
    /\ seg = [g \in Segments |-> NoOne]
    /\ latch = [b \in Books |-> NoOne]
    /\ resting = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ slow = {}

\* Coarse before fine: a member takes one segment of the sheet, and only then
\* the individual book latches inside that segment.
TakeSegment(m, g) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ seg[g] = NoOne
    /\ \A k \in Segments : seg[k] # m
    /\ seg' = [seg EXCEPT ![g] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, resting, slow>>

\* The matching engine can only follow so many books at once; a latch is a
\* book being followed, so latches are what the engine capacity limits.
TakeBook(m, b) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ seg[SegOf(b)] = m
    /\ latch[b] = NoOne
    /\ Cardinality(Latched) < Tracks
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![b] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, resting, slow>>

Rest(m, b) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ latch[b] = m
    /\ resting[b] = 0
    /\ resting' = [resting EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, latch, slow>>

DropBook(m, b) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ latch[b] = m
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, resting, slow>>

DropSegment(m, g) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ seg[g] = m
    /\ \A b \in Books : SegOf(b) = g => latch[b] # m
    /\ seg' = [seg EXCEPT ![g] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, resting, slow>>

Match(b) ==
    /\ resting[b] = 1
    /\ resting' = [resting EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, latch, slow>>

\* A member can go slow without failing: it keeps its segment and its latches,
\* it just stops doing anything with them, and nobody may take them off it.
Stall(m) ==
    /\ m \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, latch, resting>>

Resume(m) ==
    /\ m \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seg, latch, resting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, g \in Segments : TakeSegment(m, g) \/ DropSegment(m, g)
    \/ \E m \in Members, b \in Books : TakeBook(m, b) \/ Rest(m, b) \/ DropBook(m, b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Match(b)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Stall(m) \/ Resume(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The matching engine never has more books latched to it than it has tracks
\* to follow them on.
EngineTracksNotExceeded == Cardinality(Latched) <= Tracks

====
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction from a sheet divided into segments — equities in one,
bonds in another — with individual order books inside each segment. Member firms work the sheet under
a two-level locking discipline: a firm first takes a whole segment, holding one segment at a time,
and only then may it latch individual books inside the segment it holds. A segment is given back
only once the firm holds no latch inside it.

A latch is not just an exclusion: it is a book being actively followed by the matching engine, and
the engine has a fixed number of tracks. It can follow only that many books at once, and driving it
past that number is what makes it drop updates on the books it is already following. So the number
of books latched across the whole sheet must never exceed the engine's track count, and a firm
cannot take a latch when every track is already in use, however free the book itself may be.

An order is rested in a book by the firm holding that book's latch, and rests there until it is
matched away. Matching happens on its own as the auction proceeds.

A member firm can go slow without failing. A slow firm keeps its segment and its latches — it has
not crashed, its session is up, it is simply not doing anything with them for a while — and nobody
may take them off it. Its tracks stay occupied for as long as it is slow, which is exactly why the
track count binds. A slow firm resumes on its own and carries on.

The full set of actions is: TakeSegment, in which a firm holding no segment takes a free one;
TakeBook, in which a firm latches a free book inside the segment it holds, provided a track is free;
Rest, in which a firm rests an order in a book it has latched; DropBook, in which a firm gives a book
latch back; DropSegment, in which a firm holding no latch inside a segment gives that segment back;
Match, in which a resting order is matched away; Stall, in which a firm goes slow while keeping
everything it holds; and Resume, in which a slow firm comes back up to speed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of books latched across the whole sheet never exceeds the number of
tracks the matching engine has to follow them on.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bots, Docks, Horizon, MaxHold, Vacant, NoDock, NoOrder

VARIABLES lease, clock, parked, order

vars == <<lease, clock, parked, order>>

Holds == [to: Bots, until: 1 .. Horizon]

Live(d) == lease[d] # Vacant /\ lease[d].until > clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Docks -> Holds \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ parked \in [Bots -> Docks \cup {NoDock}]
    /\ order \in Docks \cup {NoOrder}

Init ==
    /\ lease = [d \in Docks |-> Vacant]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ parked = [r \in Bots |-> NoDock]
    /\ order = NoOrder

\* A charging dock is let on a lease with an expiry, and a robot holds at most
\* one live lease at a time.
Let(r, d, len) ==
    /\ ~Live(d)
    /\ \A k \in Docks : ~(Live(k) /\ lease[k].to = r)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![d] = [to |-> r, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, parked, order>>

Park(r, d) ==
    /\ parked[r] = NoDock
    /\ Live(d)
    /\ lease[d].to = r
    /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![r] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, order>>

Depart(r) ==
    /\ parked[r] # NoDock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![parked[r]] = Vacant]
    /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![r] = NoDock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, order>>

\* A robot's right to sit on a dock lapses with its lease: as the clock passes
\* the expiry it is rolled off in the same movement.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ parked' = [r \in Bots |->
                      IF parked[r] # NoDock /\ lease[parked[r]].until <= clock + 1
                      THEN NoDock ELSE parked[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, order>>

Reap(d) ==
    /\ lease[d] # Vacant
    /\ lease[d].until <= clock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![d] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, parked, order>>

\* Privileged override: the floor supervisor orders a dock cleared, and the
\* order is always acted on one way or the other.
Command(d) ==
    /\ order = NoOrder
    /\ lease[d] # Vacant
    /\ order' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, parked>>

Enforce ==
    /\ order # NoOrder
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![order] = Vacant]
    /\ parked' = [r \in Bots |-> IF parked[r] = order THEN NoDock ELSE parked[r]]
    /\ order' = NoOrder
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Rescind ==
    /\ order # NoOrder
    /\ order' = NoOrder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, parked>>

NewShift ==
    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ \A d \in Docks : lease[d] = Vacant
    /\ \A r \in Bots : parked[r] = NoDock
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, parked, order>>

Settling == Enforce \/ Rescind

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Bots, d \in Docks, n \in 1 .. MaxHold : Let(r, d, n)
    \/ \E r \in Bots, d \in Docks : Park(r, d)
    \/ \E r \in Bots : Depart(r)
    \/ \E d \in Docks : Reap(d) \/ Command(d)
    \/ Settling \/ Tick \/ NewShift

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* Every robot sitting on a dock is sitting on one whose lease names that very
\* robot and has not run out, so a dock is never allocated to two robots.
ParkedUnderLease ==
    \A r \in Bots :
        parked[r] # NoDock =>
            /\ lease[parked[r]] # Vacant
            /\ lease[parked[r]].to = r
            /\ lease[parked[r]].until > clock

\* A supervisor's clear-the-dock order never sits unanswered.
OrdersAreAnswered == (order # NoOrder) ~> (order = NoOrder)

CONSTANTS
    Bots = {btLift, btTow}
    Docks = {dkFast, dkTrickle}
    Horizon = 3
    MaxHold = 2
    Vacant = Vacant
    NoDock = NoDock
    NoOrder = NoOrder
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ParkedUnderLease
PROPERTY OrdersAreAnswered
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a small bank of charging docks. A dock takes one robot at a time, so
the fleet controller must never allocate the same dock to two robots — two machines nosing into one
charger is a bent contact and a robot out of service for a week.

Docks are let on leases with an expiry rather than handed over. A robot is let a dock for a chosen
number of minutes, provided that dock is not under a live lease, the robot does not already hold a
live lease elsewhere, and the expiry falls inside the shift. A robot only noses onto a dock against a
live lease naming it. Its right to sit there lapses with the lease: as the clock passes the expiry it
is rolled off the dock in the same movement, so nothing is ever sitting on a dock under a lease that
has run out. A robot that finishes charging departs and its lease is torn up, and leases that have
run out are reaped so the dock goes back into the pool.

The floor supervisor has a privileged override. An order can be given to clear a particular dock —
a pallet has fallen against it, an engineer needs to get at the cabinet — and the order takes effect
regardless of whose lease is on it: the lease is torn up and whatever robot is sitting there is
rolled off. Orders are never left hanging: one is always either enforced or rescinded, and only one
order stands at a time.

At the end of the shift, once no lease is outstanding and no robot is on a dock, the clock is reset.

The full set of actions is: Let, in which a robot holding no live lease is let a dock that is free,
for a period inside the shift; Park, in which a robot noses onto a dock against a live lease naming
it; Depart, in which a charged robot leaves and its lease is torn up; Tick, in which the clock
advances a minute and any robot whose lease has just run out is rolled off; Reap, in which a lease
that has run out is cleared away; Command, in which the supervisor orders a dock cleared; Enforce,
in which the order is carried out, tearing up the lease and rolling off whoever is there; Rescind, in
which the order is withdrawn; and NewShift, in which the clock is reset once nothing is leased or
parked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every robot sitting on a charging dock is on one whose lease names that very robot
and has not yet run out, so a dock is never allocated to two robots at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A supervisor's order to clear a dock never sits unanswered — it is always
eventually enforced or rescinded.

---- MODULE W4Od19m9p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Titles, Branches, MaxEpoch, MaxShelf

VARIABLES pulped, orders, cat, shelf, shelved

vars == <<pulped, orders, cat, shelf, shelved>>

Orders == [title: Titles, by: Branches, cat: 0 .. MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pulped \subseteq Titles
    /\ orders \subseteq Orders
    /\ cat \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ shelf \in 1 .. MaxShelf
    /\ shelved \in 0 .. MaxShelf

Init ==
    /\ pulped = {}
    /\ orders = {}
    /\ cat = 0
    /\ shelf = MaxShelf
    /\ shelved = 0

\* A withdrawal order is stamped with the catalogue epoch it was raised under,
\* and is never raised against a title that has already gone.
Raise(t, b) ==
    /\ t \notin pulped
    /\ \A o \in orders : ~(o.title = t /\ o.by = b)
    /\ orders' = orders \cup {[title |-> t, by |-> b, cat |-> cat]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, cat, shelf, shelved>>

\* Pulping is one-way: the copies are shredded. Every other branch's order for
\* that title goes in the same movement, so nothing can present it again.
Pulp(o) ==
    /\ o \in orders
    /\ o.cat = cat
    /\ pulped' = pulped \cup {o.title}
    /\ orders' = {q \in orders : q.title # o.title}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cat, shelf, shelved>>

Withdraw(o) ==
    /\ o \in orders
    /\ orders' = orders \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, cat, shelf, shelved>>

Purge(o) ==
    /\ o \in orders
    /\ o.cat # cat
    /\ orders' = orders \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, cat, shelf, shelved>>

Reserve ==
    /\ shelved < shelf
    /\ shelved' = shelved + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, orders, cat, shelf>>

Collect ==
    /\ shelved > 0
    /\ shelved' = shelved - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, orders, cat, shelf>>

\* Recataloguing renumbers the epoch and resizes the hold shelf at runtime,
\* never below what is already sitting on it.
Recatalogue(n) ==
    /\ cat < MaxEpoch
    /\ n >= shelved
    /\ cat' = cat + 1
    /\ shelf' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pulped, orders, shelved>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Titles, b \in Branches : Raise(t, b)
    \/ \E o \in orders : Pulp(o) \/ Withdraw(o) \/ Purge(o)
    \/ Reserve \/ Collect
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxShelf : Recatalogue(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No withdrawal order is ever left standing against a title that has already
\* been pulped, so the one-way act can never be carried out on it twice.
NoOrderForPulped ==
    \A o \in orders : o.title \notin pulped

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Titles = {tiAtlas, tiPoems}
    Branches = {brCentral, brRiverside}
    MaxEpoch = 1
    MaxShelf = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoOrderForPulped
nl:
A library group runs reservations and stock control across several branches from one catalogue.
Withdrawing a title is the one act it cannot take back: the copies go to the pulper, and a title
withdrawn twice means a second branch's stock shredded on the strength of a request that was already
carried out. So a withdrawal must happen to a title once and once only.

The catalogue is numbered by epoch. A branch raises a withdrawal order for a title that has not
already gone, and the order is stamped with the catalogue epoch it was raised under. A branch raises
at most one order per title. An order is only carried out while its stamp matches the running epoch:
an order from an earlier catalogue may be pointing at a record that has since been merged or
renumbered, so it is never acted on and is purged instead. Orders can also simply be withdrawn by
the branch that raised them.

When an order is carried out, the title is pulped and every other branch's order for that same title
goes with it, so no second order can ever be presented for it.

The hold shelf has a capacity that changes while the service runs. Reservations go onto the shelf
while there is room and come off when readers collect them. Recataloguing advances the epoch and
resizes the hold shelf at the same time, never below the number of reservations already sitting on
it.

The full set of actions is: Raise, in which a branch raises a withdrawal order, stamped with the
running epoch, for a title that has not been pulped and that it has not already ordered; Pulp, in
which an order whose stamp matches the running epoch is carried out, pulping the title and clearing
every order for it; Withdraw, in which a branch takes its own order back; Purge, in which an order
stamped with an earlier epoch is cleared away unacted on; Reserve, in which a reservation goes onto
the hold shelf while there is room; Collect, in which a reader takes a reservation off the shelf; and
Recatalogue, in which the catalogue epoch advances and the hold shelf is resized, never below what
is already on it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No withdrawal order is ever left standing against a title that has already been
pulped, so the one-way act can never be carried out on the same title twice.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Capacity, MaxVer, NoPlan

VARIABLES onLine, ver, planApp, planKiosk

vars == <<onLine, ver, planApp, planKiosk>>

Plans == [saw: 0 .. MaxVer, count: 0 .. Capacity]

Fits(p) == p # NoPlan /\ p.saw = ver /\ p.count < Capacity /\ ver < MaxVer

TypeOK ==
    /\ onLine \in 0 .. Capacity
    /\ ver \in 0 .. MaxVer
    /\ planApp \in Plans \cup {NoPlan}
    /\ planKiosk \in Plans \cup {NoPlan}

Init ==
    /\ onLine = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ planApp = NoPlan
    /\ planKiosk = NoPlan

\* The phone app.  It reads the line counter and its version, works out the
\* booking off-line, and only then tries to write.
ReadApp ==
    /\ planApp = NoPlan
    /\ planApp' = [saw |-> ver, count |-> onLine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ver, planKiosk>>

CommitApp ==
    /\ Fits(planApp)
    /\ onLine' = planApp.count + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ planApp' = NoPlan
    /\ UNCHANGED planKiosk

ClashApp ==
    /\ planApp # NoPlan
    /\ ~Fits(planApp)
    /\ planApp' = NoPlan
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ver, planKiosk>>

\* The forecourt kiosk.  Separate box, separate code, same line counter.
ReadKiosk ==
    /\ planKiosk = NoPlan
    /\ planKiosk' = [saw |-> ver, count |-> onLine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ver, planApp>>

CommitKiosk ==
    /\ Fits(planKiosk)
    /\ onLine' = planKiosk.count + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ planKiosk' = NoPlan
    /\ UNCHANGED planApp

ClashKiosk ==
    /\ planKiosk # NoPlan
    /\ ~Fits(planKiosk)
    /\ planKiosk' = NoPlan
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ver, planApp>>

Roll ==
    /\ onLine > 0
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ onLine' = onLine - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<planApp, planKiosk>>

\* The version counter is renumbered between sessions, with nothing in flight,
\* so a stale read can never be mistaken for a current one.
Renumber ==
    /\ ver = MaxVer
    /\ planApp = NoPlan
    /\ planKiosk = NoPlan
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, planApp, planKiosk>>

ResolveApp == CommitApp \/ ClashApp
ResolveKiosk == CommitKiosk \/ ClashKiosk

Next ==
    \/ ReadApp \/ ResolveApp
    \/ ReadKiosk \/ ResolveKiosk
    \/ Roll \/ Renumber

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ResolveApp) /\ WF_vars(ResolveKiosk)

\* The conveyor never carries more cars than it has room for, and any booking
\* still holding a current version read the count that is actually on the line.
CapacityRespected ==
    /\ onLine <= Capacity
    /\ (planApp # NoPlan /\ planApp.saw = ver) => planApp.count = onLine
    /\ (planKiosk # NoPlan /\ planKiosk.saw = ver) => planKiosk.count = onLine

\* Neither booking system leaves a half-finished booking hanging.
BookingsSettle ==
    /\ (planApp # NoPlan) ~> (planApp = NoPlan)
    /\ (planKiosk # NoPlan) ~> (planKiosk = NoPlan)

CONSTANTS
    Capacity = 2
    MaxVer = 3
    NoPlan = NoPlan
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
PROPERTY BookingsSettle
nl:
A car wash pulls cars along a conveyor that holds only so many at once. Two booking systems put cars
onto it — the chain's phone app and the forecourt kiosk — and they were written by different
suppliers with no link between them beyond the line counter itself. Overfilling the conveyor jams
the rails, so the number of cars on the line must never exceed what it can hold.

Neither system locks the counter. Each reads the counter along with its version number, works out
its booking off-line, and only then tries to write back. The write goes through only if the version
is still the one it read, the count it read leaves room on the line, and the version counter has not
run to the end of its range; the write then bumps the version. If the version moved while the
booking was being worked out — because the other system got in first — or the line was already full,
the attempt clashes and the system starts again from a fresh read. Neither system leaves a
half-finished booking hanging: an attempt is always either written or clashed.

Cars come off the far end of the line as they finish, which drops the count and bumps the version
too. The version counter is renumbered back to the start between sessions, and only while neither
system has a read outstanding, so a stale read can never be mistaken for a current one by the
numbering coming round again.

The full set of actions is: ReadApp and ReadKiosk, in which the system concerned takes a copy of the
line count and version; CommitApp and CommitKiosk, in which the write goes through because the
version is unmoved, the count read leaves room and the version range is not exhausted, putting a car
on the line and bumping the version; ClashApp and ClashKiosk, in which the attempt is dropped
because any of those checks failed; Roll, in which a car comes off the end of the line, dropping the
count and bumping the version; and Renumber, in which the version counter goes back to the start
with nothing in flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The conveyor never carries more cars than it has room for, and any booking still
holding a current version number read the count that is actually on the line.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Neither booking system is ever left with an attempt hanging: every read is
eventually either written or clashed.

---- MODULE W4Od18m4p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Hubs, Fobs, QCap, Free, NoFob

VARIABLES work, burning, burnt, claim

vars == <<work, burning, burnt, claim>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ \A h \in Hubs : Len(work[h]) <= QCap
    /\ \A h \in Hubs : \A i \in 1 .. Len(work[h]) : work[h][i] \in Fobs
    /\ burning \in [Hubs -> Fobs \cup {NoFob}]
    /\ burnt \subseteq Fobs
    /\ claim \in [Fobs -> Hubs \cup {Free}]

Init ==
    /\ work = [h \in Hubs |-> <<>>]
    /\ burning = [h \in Hubs |-> NoFob]
    /\ burnt = {}
    /\ claim = [f \in Fobs |-> Free]

\* Backpressure: a hub stops accepting pairing requests once its queue is full.
Accept(h, f) ==
    /\ Len(work[h]) < QCap
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![h] = Append(@, f)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burning, burnt, claim>>

\* The registrar hands the fob to one hub at a time; the other hub's request
\* for the same fob is dropped rather than queued behind it.
Begin(h) ==
    /\ work[h] # <<>>
    /\ burning[h] = NoFob
    /\ Head(work[h]) \notin burnt
    /\ claim[Head(work[h])] = Free
    /\ burning' = [burning EXCEPT ![h] = Head(work[h])]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![Head(work[h])] = h]
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![h] = Tail(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED burnt

Skip(h) ==
    /\ work[h] # <<>>
    /\ \/ Head(work[h]) \in burnt
       \/ claim[Head(work[h])] # Free
       \/ burning[h] # NoFob
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![h] = Tail(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burning, burnt, claim>>

\* Burning the fob blows the one-time slot: there is no unburning it.
Burn(h) ==
    /\ burning[h] # NoFob
    /\ burnt' = burnt \cup {burning[h]}
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![burning[h]] = Free]
    /\ burning' = [burning EXCEPT ![h] = NoFob]
    /\ UNCHANGED work

Abandon(h) ==
    /\ burning[h] # NoFob
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![burning[h]] = Free]
    /\ burning' = [burning EXCEPT ![h] = NoFob]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<work, burnt>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs, f \in Fobs : Accept(h, f)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Begin(h) \/ Skip(h) \/ Burn(h) \/ Abandon(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A hub is only ever part-way through burning a fob that has not been burnt
\* already and that the registrar has handed to that same hub, so the one-time
\* slot can never be blown twice.
BurnIsExclusive ==
    \A h \in Hubs :
        burning[h] # NoFob => (burning[h] \notin burnt /\ claim[burning[h]] = h)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Hubs = {hbCloud, hbBridge}
    Fobs = {fbFront, fbGarage}
    QCap = 2
    Free = Free
    NoFob = NoFob
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BurnIsExclusive
nl:
A smart-home door lock network pairs key fobs to locks. Pairing a fob blows a one-time slot in the
fob's secure element: the write cannot be reversed, and blowing the same fob's slot twice bricks it,
leaving the householder locked out. So a fob must be burnt once and once only.

Two hubs drive the same pool of fobs and neither was written with the other in mind: the vendor's
cloud hub and the local bridge that keeps working when the internet is down. Each hub has its own
bounded queue of pairing requests and applies backpressure — once a hub's queue is at its cap it
stops accepting requests, and the household app has to try again later.

The fob registrar is what keeps the two hubs apart. A hub takes the request at the head of its queue
and begins burning only if the fob has not already been burnt and the registrar shows it unclaimed,
and beginning claims it for that hub. If the fob is already burnt, or already claimed by the other
hub, or the hub is already part-way through a burn of its own, the request is dropped from the queue
rather than left to sit behind. When the burn completes the slot is blown for good and the claim is
released. A hub can also abandon a burn part-way through, which releases the claim with the slot
still unblown.

The full set of actions is: Accept, in which a hub takes a pairing request onto the tail of its queue
while the queue is below its cap; Begin, in which a hub starts burning the fob at the head of its
queue, having found it unburnt and unclaimed, and claims it; Skip, in which the request at the head

already burning something; Burn, in which the one-time slot is blown and the claim released; and
Abandon, in which a hub gives up part-way through and releases the claim.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any hub part-way through a burn is working on a fob that has not already been burnt
and that the registrar has claimed for that same hub, so a fob's one-time slot can never be blown
twice.

    /\ at \in [Cranes -> Cells \cup {NoCell}]
    /\ bid \in [Cranes -> Cells \cup {NoBid}]
    /\ shift \in 0 .. MaxShift

    /\ reg = [k \in Cells |-> Free]
    /\ at = [c \in Cranes |-> NoCell]
    /\ bid = [c \in Cranes |-> NoBid]
    /\ shift = 0

Aim(c, k) ==
    /\ bid[c] = NoBid
    /\ at[c] = NoCell
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, at, shift>>

\* The compare-and-swap on the cell register: it lands only if the register
\* still reads free, and it writes both sides of the booking in one step.
Swap(c) ==
    /\ bid[c] # NoBid
    /\ at[c] = NoCell
    /\ reg[bid[c]] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![bid[c]] = c]
    /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![c] = bid[c]]
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![c] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED shift

Miss(c) ==
    /\ bid[c] # NoBid
    /\ \/ reg[bid[c]] # Free
       \/ at[c] # NoCell
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![c] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, at, shift>>

Quit(c) ==
    /\ at[c] # NoCell
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![at[c]] = Free]
    /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![c] = NoCell]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bid, shift>>

\* register at once, whoever is on it, and the shift number rolls on.

    /\ reg' = [k \in Cells |-> Free]
    /\ at' = [c \in Cranes |-> NoCell]

    /\ UNCHANGED bid

    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Swap(c) \/ Miss(c) \/ Quit(c)
    \/ YardClear

\* back, and a booked cell's crane is standing on that very cell, so no cell is
\* ever allocated to two cranes.

CONSTANTS

    MaxShift = 2
    Free = Free
    NoCell = NoCell
    NoBid = NoBid

INVARIANT BookingsAgree
PROPERTY YardEmpties
nl:
A container terminal parcels its stacking ground into cells and lets its cranes book them directly,
with no yard planner in the middle. A cell takes one crane's work at a time: two cranes booked onto
the same cell means two spreaders swinging into the same stack.

Each cell carries a register that reads free or names the crane working it. A crane picks a cell it
wants and then attempts a compare-and-swap on that register: the attempt lands only if the register
still reads free at that instant, and when it lands it writes both sides of the booking in one step —
the register takes the crane's name and the crane records the cell it is standing on. If the register
is no longer free, or the crane has been given a cell in the meantime, the attempt is missed and
dropped. A crane quits a cell when it has finished, clearing both sides again.

The yard master has a privileged override. At the end of a shift the whole register is cleared at
once — every booking on it, whoever holds it, with no notice to the cranes — and the shift number
rolls on, wrapping at the top of its range. That sweep always happens, so no cell stays booked
indefinitely.

The full set of actions is: Aim, in which a crane with no bid outstanding and no cell of its own
picks a cell to go for; Swap, in which the compare-and-swap lands because the register still reads
free, writing the crane into the register and the cell into the crane's record; Miss, in which the
attempt is dropped because the register is no longer free or the crane already has a cell; Quit, in
which a crane gives up the cell it holds and both sides are cleared; and YardClear, in which the yard
master clears the entire register and every crane's record at once and the shift number rolls on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The two sides of every booking agree — a crane's recorded cell names that crane back
in its register, and every booked cell's named crane is recorded as standing on that very cell — so
a cell is never allocated to two cranes at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The yard is always eventually cleared down: no cell stays booked for ever.

CONSTANTS Bags, Stands, QCap, Empty

VARIABLES stand, belt, offline, closed

vars == <<stand, belt, offline, closed>>

Intents == [bag: Bags, pos: Stands]

Queued(p) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : belt[i].pos = p

TypeOK ==
    /\ stand \in [Stands -> Bags \cup {Empty}]
    /\ Len(belt) <= QCap
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : belt[i] \in Intents
    /\ offline \subseteq Stands
    /\ closed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ stand = [p \in Stands |-> Empty]
    /\ belt = <<>>
    /\ offline = {}
    /\ closed = FALSE

\* Backpressure, plus the rule that keeps allocation single: a stand with a bag
\* on it, or with an intent already queued against it, is not planned again.
Plan(b, p) ==
    /\ ~closed
    /\ Len(belt) < QCap
    /\ stand[p] = Empty
    /\ ~Queued(p)
    /\ p \notin offline
    /\ \A q \in Stands : stand[q] # b
    /\ belt' = Append(belt, [bag |-> b, pos |-> p])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stand, offline, closed>>

Route ==
    /\ belt # <<>>
    /\ stand[Head(belt).pos] = Empty
    /\ Head(belt).pos \notin offline
    /\ stand' = [stand EXCEPT ![Head(belt).pos] = Head(belt).bag]
    /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<offline, closed>>

Bounce ==
    /\ belt # <<>>
    /\ \/ stand[Head(belt).pos] # Empty
       \/ Head(belt).pos \in offline
    /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stand, offline, closed>>

Loaded(p) ==
    /\ stand[p] # Empty
    /\ stand' = [stand EXCEPT ![p] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, offline, closed>>

\* Privileged override: the duty manager pulls a stand out of service or hauls
\* a bag off it, without going near the belt.
TakeOut(p) ==
    /\ p \notin offline
    /\ offline' = offline \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stand, belt, closed>>

PutBack(p) ==
    /\ p \in offline
    /\ offline' = offline \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stand, belt, closed>>

Haul(p) ==
    /\ stand[p] # Empty
    /\ stand' = [stand EXCEPT ![p] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, offline, closed>>

Shut ==
    /\ closed' = ~closed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stand, belt, offline>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, p \in Stands : Plan(b, p)
    \/ Route \/ Bounce \/ Shut
    \/ \E p \in Stands : Loaded(p) \/ TakeOut(p) \/ PutBack(p) \/ Haul(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing on the routing belt is addressed to a make-up stand that already has
\* a bag on it, so a stand is never allocated to two bags at once.
NoQueuedOnTakenStand ==
    \A i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : stand[belt[i].pos] = Empty

CONSTANTS
    Bags = {bgHold, bgTransfer}
    Stands = {stEast, stWest}
    QCap = 2
    Empty = Empty
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoQueuedOnTakenStand
nl:
An airport baggage router sends bags to make-up stands, one stand per departing flight's build. A
stand takes one bag's build at a time: allocating the same stand to two bags puts two flights' loads
into one cart and sends somebody's suitcase to the wrong continent.

Routing decisions queue on a bounded belt with backpressure. A plan is put on the tail of the belt
only while the belt is below its cap, and only for a stand that has no bag on it, has no plan already
queued against it, and is in service; the bag itself must not already be standing anywhere. That
combination — one plan per stand and no plan for an occupied stand — is what keeps allocation
single.

The belt is worked from the front. The plan at the head is routed if its stand is still empty and
still in service, which puts the bag on the stand and takes the plan off the belt. If the stand has
been taken in the meantime, or pulled out of service, the plan is bounced off the belt instead. Bags
leave stands the ordinary way when the build is loaded onto the aircraft.

The duty manager has a privileged override and works outside the belt entirely. A stand can be
pulled out of service and put back later; a bag can be hauled straight off a stand; and the belt can
be closed to new plans altogether and reopened.

The full set of actions is: Plan, in which a routing plan for a free, in-service stand joins the tail
of the belt while the belt is open and below its cap; Route, in which the plan at the head is carried
out, putting the bag on the stand; Bounce, in which the plan at the head is thrown off because its
stand was taken or pulled out of service; Loaded, in which a built bag leaves its stand for the
aircraft; TakeOut and PutBack, in which the duty manager pulls a stand out of service and returns it;
Haul, in which the duty manager takes a bag straight off a stand; and Shut, in which the duty manager
closes the belt to new plans or reopens it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Nothing sitting on the routing belt is addressed to a make-up stand that already has
a bag on it, so a stand is never allocated to two bags at once.

CONSTANTS Techs, Scripts, MaxVer, MaxPolicy, NoDraft

VARIABLES rev, policy, badge, roster, draft

vars == <<rev, policy, badge, roster, draft>>

Drafts == [tech: Techs, script: Scripts, saw: 0 .. MaxVer]

Roll(v, top) == IF v = top THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ rev \in [Scripts -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ policy \in 0 .. MaxPolicy
    /\ badge \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxPolicy]
    /\ roster \subseteq Techs
    /\ draft \in Drafts \cup {NoDraft}

Init ==
    /\ rev = [s \in Scripts |-> 0]
    /\ policy = 0
    /\ badge = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
    /\ roster = Techs
    /\ draft = NoDraft

\* No lock is taken: the technician notes the revision the script is on and
\* goes off to make the preparation up.
Prepare(t, s) ==
    /\ draft = NoDraft
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ badge[t] = policy
    /\ draft' = [tech |-> t, script |-> s, saw |-> rev[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, policy, badge, roster>>

\* Handing over annotates the script, which rolls its revision on.
Dispense ==
    /\ draft # NoDraft
    /\ draft.saw = rev[draft.script]
    /\ draft.tech \in roster
    /\ badge[draft.tech] = policy
    /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![draft.script] = Roll(@, MaxVer)]
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, badge, roster>>

Abandon ==
    /\ draft # NoDraft
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, policy, badge, roster>>

\* Anything that could leave the bench working from a superseded picture tears
\* the draft up in the same movement.
Amend(s) ==
    /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@, MaxVer)]
    /\ draft' = IF draft # NoDraft /\ draft.script = s THEN NoDraft ELSE draft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, badge, roster>>

TurnPolicy ==
    /\ policy' = Roll(policy, MaxPolicy)
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, badge, roster>>

Rebadge(t) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ badge[t] # policy
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![t] = policy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, policy, roster, draft>>

\* Privileged override: the pharmacist strikes a technician off mid-shift and
\* whatever they had on the bench goes with them.
StrikeOff(t) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ roster' = roster \ {t}
    /\ draft' = IF draft # NoDraft /\ draft.tech = t THEN NoDraft ELSE draft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, policy, badge>>

Reinstate(t) ==
    /\ t \notin roster
    /\ roster' = roster \cup {t}
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, policy, draft>>

Settling == Dispense \/ Abandon

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs, s \in Scripts : Prepare(t, s)
    \/ Settling \/ TurnPolicy
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : Amend(s)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Rebadge(t) \/ StrikeOff(t) \/ Reinstate(t)

\* the roster, carrying the current policy badge, and was worked up from the
\* revision the script is still on.
BenchIsCurrent ==
    draft # NoDraft =>
        /\ draft.tech \in roster
        /\ badge[draft.tech] = policy
        /\ draft.saw = rev[draft.script]

\* Nothing is left half-made on the bench.
BenchClears == (draft # NoDraft) ~> (draft = NoDraft)

CONSTANTS
    Techs = {tcRow, tcNair}
    Scripts = {scInsulin, scWarfarin}
    MaxVer = 1
    MaxPolicy = 1
    NoDraft = NoDraft
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BenchIsCurrent
PROPERTY BenchClears
nl:
A hospital pharmacy dispenses against electronic prescriptions. Each prescription carries a revision
number that rolls on every time the script is annotated or amended, and every technician carries a
policy badge that has to match the pharmacy's current policy generation. The safety case is about
who did the work and against what: nothing may be made up by a technician who has been struck off,
nor by one carrying a superseded badge, nor from a revision of the script that has since been
changed.

The bench takes no locks. A technician notes the revision the script is currently on and goes off to
make the preparation up; the script stays open to amendment the whole time. Only one preparation is
on the bench at a time. Handing the medication over is what commits it: the script is annotated,
which rolls its revision on, and the bench is cleared. A technician can also simply abandon a
preparation. Nothing is ever left half-made — a preparation on the bench is always eventually either
handed over or abandoned.

Anything that would leave the bench working from a picture that has been superseded tears the draft
up in the same movement. Amending a script tears up a draft made from it. Turning the policy
generation, which invalidates every badge at once, tears up whatever is on the bench. A technician
still on the roster can re-badge to the current generation and start again.

The pharmacist has a privileged override on individuals: a technician can be struck off mid-shift,
and whatever they had on the bench goes with them. Somebody struck off can be reinstated later, but
comes back with a zeroed badge and has to re-badge before they can work.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a rostered, correctly badged technician notes a
script's revision and starts making it up on the empty bench; Dispense, in which the preparation is
handed over, the script annotated and its revision rolled on; Abandon, in which the preparation is
given up; Amend, in which a script's revision rolls on and any draft made from it is torn up;
TurnPolicy, in which the policy generation turns and the bench is cleared; Rebadge, in which a
rostered technician refreshes a stale badge; StrikeOff, in which the pharmacist removes a technician
from the roster and tears up their draft; and Reinstate, in which a struck-off technician returns
with a zeroed badge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Anything sitting on the dispensing bench belongs to a technician still on the
roster, carrying the current policy badge, and was worked up from the revision the script is still
on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Nothing is left half-made — every preparation on the bench is eventually either
handed over or abandoned.

vars == <<group, carried, armed, prop, ayes, shed>>

Props == [by: Relays, feeder: Feeders]

InSync == {r \in Relays : r \in armed /\ carried[r] = group}

TypeOK ==
    /\ group \in 0 .. MaxGroup
    /\ carried \in [Relays -> 0 .. MaxGroup]
    /\ armed \subseteq Relays
    /\ prop \in Props \cup {NoProp}
    /\ ayes \subseteq Relays
    /\ shed \subseteq Feeders

Init ==
    /\ group = 0
    /\ carried = [r \in Relays |-> 0]
    /\ armed = Relays
    /\ prop = NoProp
    /\ ayes = {}
    /\ shed = {}

\* Only a relay armed and carrying the running settings group may open a round.
Propose(r, f) ==
    /\ prop = NoProp
    /\ r \in InSync
    /\ f \notin shed
    /\ prop' = [by |-> r, feeder |-> f]
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, shed>>

Aye(r) ==
    /\ prop # NoProp
    /\ r \in InSync
    /\ r \notin ayes
    /\ ayes' = ayes \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, shed>>

Commit ==
    /\ prop # NoProp
    /\ InSync \subseteq ayes
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {prop.feeder}
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed>>

Abort ==
    /\ prop # NoProp
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, shed>>

Reclose(f) ==
    /\ f \in shed
    /\ shed' = shed \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, ayes>>

\* A new settings group supersedes every relay's copy at once, so any round in
\* flight is torn down rather than carried across the change.
Publish ==
    /\ group' = IF group = MaxGroup THEN 0 ELSE group + 1
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, armed, shed>>

Adopt(r) ==
    /\ carried[r] # group
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = group]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, armed, prop, ayes, shed>>

\* its vote with it and dropping any round it was running.
Disarm(r) ==

    /\ armed' = armed \ {r}
    /\ ayes' = ayes \ {r}
    /\ prop' = IF prop # NoProp /\ prop.by = r THEN NoProp ELSE prop
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, shed>>

Rearm(r) ==
    /\ r \notin armed
    /\ armed' = armed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, prop, ayes, shed>>

ForceShed(f) ==
    /\ f \notin shed
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, ayes>>

CONSTANTS

    Feeders = {fdMill, fdTown}
    MaxGroup = 1
    NoProp = NoProp

INVARIANT RoundIsInSync
nl:
A regional grid sheds load by agreement between its protection relays rather than on one relay's say
so. Opening a feeder is decided by two-phase commit: a relay opens a round on a feeder that is still
closed, the relays vote, and the feeder opens once everybody eligible has voted in favour.

Eligibility is what the safety case turns on. Every relay carries a copy of the protection settings
group, and the grid publishes a running group number. A relay counts only while it is armed and its
copy matches the published group: a relay that has been disarmed is not part of the scheme at all,
and a relay still carrying a superseded settings group is reasoning from trip thresholds that have
been replaced. Neither may open a round and neither may have its vote counted.

Publishing a new settings group supersedes every relay's copy at once, so any round in flight is
torn down rather than carried across the change. A relay brings its copy up to the published group
by adopting it, and can then take part again. Feeders that have been opened are reclosed as demand
recovers.

The control room has a privileged override on both halves. A relay can be disarmed on the spot: its
vote is pulled out of the round and, if it was the relay running the round, the round is dropped
altogether. A disarmed relay can be rearmed later. The control room can also open a feeder outright,
with no round and no vote at all.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which an armed, in-group relay opens a round on a closed
feeder and clears the tally; Aye, in which an armed, in-group relay adds its vote to the round;
Commit, in which every eligible relay having voted in favour opens the feeder and closes the round;
Abort, in which the round is dropped with nothing opened; Reclose, in which an opened feeder is
closed again; Publish, in which a new settings group is issued and any round in flight is torn down;
Adopt, in which a relay brings its copy up to the published group; Disarm, in which the control room
disarms a relay, pulling its vote and dropping any round it was running; Rearm, in which a disarmed
relay is brought back into the scheme; and ForceShed, in which the control room opens a feeder
outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any round in flight is being run by a relay that is armed and carrying the
published settings group, and every vote behind it comes from such a relay, so nobody disarmed and
nobody on a superseded settings group is ever part of a shedding decision.

VARIABLES area, latch, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling

vars == <<area, latch, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling>>

Hands == Cabins \cup {NoOne}

TypeOK ==
    /\ area \in Hands
    /\ latch \in [Junctions -> Hands]
    /\ rev \in [Junctions -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ lastBase \in [Junctions -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ snap \in [Cabins -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ dawdling \subseteq Cabins

Init ==
    /\ area = NoOne
    /\ latch = [j \in Junctions |-> NoOne]
    /\ rev = [j \in Junctions |-> 0]
    /\ lastBase = [j \in Junctions |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [c \in Cabins |-> 0]
    /\ dawdling = {}

\* Coarse before fine: the area panel admits one cabin, which may then hold a
\* single junction latch.
TakeArea(c) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ area = NoOne
    /\ area' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling>>

TakeLatch(c, j) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ area = c
    /\ latch[j] = NoOne
    /\ \A k \in Junctions : latch[k] = NoOne
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![j] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling>>

\* Reads are taken without any latch at all, which is how a cabin can end up
\* holding a revision number that has moved on by the time it writes.
Read(c, j) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = rev[j]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, latch, rev, lastBase, dawdling>>

Write(c, j) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ latch[j] = c
    /\ snap[c] = rev[j]
    /\ rev[j] < MaxRev
    /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![j] = @ + 1]
    /\ lastBase' = [lastBase EXCEPT ![j] = snap[c]]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = rev[j] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, latch, dawdling>>

Release(c, j) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ latch[j] = c
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![j] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling>>

DropArea(c) ==
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ area = c
    /\ \A j \in Junctions : latch[j] # c
    /\ area' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, rev, lastBase, snap, dawdling>>

\* The cabin working the area can go slow without failing: it holds on to
\* everything and simply stops for a while, and it always comes back.
Dawdle(c) ==
    /\ area = c
    /\ c \notin dawdling
    /\ dawdling' = dawdling \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, latch, rev, lastBase, snap>>

CatchUp(c) ==
    /\ c \in dawdling
    /\ dawdling' = dawdling \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, latch, rev, lastBase, snap>>

Archive(j) ==
    /\ rev[j] = MaxRev
    /\ latch[j] = NoOne
    /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![j] = 0]
    /\ lastBase' = [lastBase EXCEPT ![j] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<area, latch, snap, dawdling>>

Releasing == \E c \in Cabins, j \in Junctions : Release(c, j)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cabins : TakeArea(c) \/ DropArea(c) \/ Dawdle(c) \/ CatchUp(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cabins, j \in Junctions : TakeLatch(c, j) \/ Read(c, j) \/ Write(c, j)
    \/ Releasing
    \/ \E j \in Junctions : Archive(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Waking) /\ SF_vars(Releasing)

\* Every revision of a junction record was written from the revision
\* immediately before it, so no cabin's edit was ever laid down over one it
\* had not read.
WritesAreContiguous ==
    \A j \in Junctions : rev[j] > 0 => lastBase[j] = rev[j] - 1

\* No junction latch is held for ever, even by a cabin that has gone slow.
LatchesRelease ==
    (\E j \in Junctions : latch[j] # NoOne) ~> (\A j \in Junctions : latch[j] = NoOne)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cabins = {cbUpper, cbLower}
    Junctions = {jnFork, jnDepot}
    MaxRev = 2
    NoOne = NoOne
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WritesAreContiguous
PROPERTY LatchesRelease
nl:
A subway line keeps a route-plan record for each junction, and the records are versioned: every
edit rolls the revision on. Two signalling cabins edit them. The hazard is a lost update — a cabin
writing an edit it worked out from a revision that has since been replaced, silently wiping what the
other cabin just wrote.

Editing is done under two levels of lock. A cabin first takes the area panel, which admits one cabin
at a time, and only then may it latch a junction, and only one junction anywhere on the line is
latched at a time. The area panel is given back once the cabin holds no latch.

Reads are deliberately not locked. A cabin can read a junction's revision number at any moment,
without holding anything, and go away and work out its edit from it. That is exactly how it can end
up holding a revision number that has moved on by the time it gets the latch. So the write is
checked: an edit only lands if the revision the cabin is holding is still the revision the record is
on. Every edit that lands records the revision it was worked out from. When a record reaches the end
of its revision range it is archived and starts again from zero.

A cabin working the area can go slow without failing. It keeps the area panel and its latch and
simply stops for a while — nobody may take them off it, because it has not failed and will come back
of its own accord. It always does come back, and no junction latch is held for ever.

The full set of actions is: TakeArea, in which a cabin that is not slow takes the free area panel;
TakeLatch, in which the cabin on the area latches a junction while no junction anywhere is latched;
Read, in which any cabin reads a junction's revision number without holding anything; Write, in
which the cabin holding a junction's latch lands an edit, provided the revision it read is still the
one the record is on, recording the revision it was worked out from; Release, in which a cabin gives
a junction latch back; DropArea, in which a cabin holding no latch gives the area panel back;
Dawdle, in which the cabin on the area goes slow while holding everything; CatchUp, in which a slow
cabin comes back up to speed; and Archive, in which an unlatched record at the end of its revision
range starts again from zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every revision of a junction record records as its base the revision immediately
before it, so no cabin's edit was ever laid down over a revision it had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No junction latch is held for ever, even by a cabin that has gone slow.
