---- MODULE W4Od17m2p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bays, Parties, TotalBags, MaxBatch, NoTxn

VARIABLES hold, txn, ballot, frozen

vars == <<hold, txn, ballot, frozen>>

Txns == [src: Bays, dst: Bays, qty: 1 .. MaxBatch]

RECURSIVE Piled(_)
Piled(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN hold[b] + Piled(S \ {b})

Escrowed == IF txn = NoTxn THEN 0 ELSE txn.qty

TypeOK ==
    /\ hold \in [Bays -> 0 .. TotalBags]
    /\ txn \in Txns \cup {NoTxn}
    /\ ballot \in [Parties -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ frozen \subseteq Bays

Init ==
    /\ hold = [b \in Bays |-> IF b = CHOOSE x \in Bays : TRUE THEN TotalBags ELSE 0]
    /\ txn = NoTxn
    /\ ballot = [p \in Parties |-> "none"]
    /\ frozen = {}

\* Preparing lifts the bags out of the source bay straight away: they sit in
\* the router's escrow for the length of the round, in neither bay.
Prepare(s, d, q) ==
    /\ txn = NoTxn
    /\ s # d
    /\ s \notin frozen
    /\ d \notin frozen
    /\ q <= hold[s]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = @ - q]
    /\ txn' = [src |-> s, dst |-> d, qty |-> q]
    /\ ballot' = [p \in Parties |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED frozen

Aye(p) ==
    /\ txn # NoTxn
    /\ ballot[p] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, frozen>>

Nay(p) ==
    /\ txn # NoTxn
    /\ ballot[p] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, frozen>>

Commit ==
    /\ txn # NoTxn
    /\ \A p \in Parties : ballot[p] = "yes"
    /\ txn.dst \notin frozen
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![txn.dst] = @ + txn.qty]
    /\ txn' = NoTxn
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, frozen>>

Rollback ==
    /\ txn # NoTxn
    /\ \/ \E p \in Parties : ballot[p] = "no"
       \/ txn.dst \in frozen
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![txn.src] = @ + txn.qty]
    /\ txn' = NoTxn
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, frozen>>

\* Privileged override: the duty manager freezes a bay, or carries bags across
\* by hand with no round and no vote at all.
Freeze(b) ==
    /\ b \notin frozen
    /\ frozen' = frozen \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, ballot>>

Thaw(b) ==
    /\ b \in frozen
    /\ frozen' = frozen \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, ballot>>

Carry(s, d, q) ==
    /\ s # d
    /\ q <= hold[s]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = @ - q, ![d] = @ + q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, ballot, frozen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s, d \in Bays, q \in 1 .. MaxBatch : Prepare(s, d, q) \/ Carry(s, d, q)
    \/ \E p \in Parties : Aye(p) \/ Nay(p)
    \/ Commit \/ Rollback
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Freeze(b) \/ Thaw(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bags only ever move between a bay and the router's escrow, so the bags piled
\* in the bays plus the batch in escrow always come to the terminal's total.
BagsConserved == Piled(Bays) + Escrowed = TotalBags

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {byTransfer, byOutbound}
    Parties = {ptSorter, ptApron}
    TotalBags = 2
    MaxBatch = 2
    NoTxn = NoTxn
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BagsConserved
nl:
An airport baggage router shifts bags between holding bays. The terminal counts bags at the start of
every shift and the count has to hold: a bag that vanishes from the system is a bag on the wrong
aircraft, and a bag that appears from nowhere is a double-count that hides the first mistake. So the
bags piled in the bays plus anything the router is holding mid-move must always come to the
terminal's total.

Moves are agreed by two-phase commit between the parties that have to sign them off, the sorter
control and the apron desk. Preparing a move lifts the batch out of the source bay straight away and
puts it into the router's escrow, where it sits for the length of the round — out of the source bay
and not yet in the destination. Each party then casts one vote. If both vote in favour, and the
destination is still open, the batch is committed into the destination bay and escrow is emptied. A
vote against, or the destination being frozen while the round is running, rolls the batch back into
the bay it came from. Either way the batch leaves escrow exactly as it arrived. Only one round is
in flight at a time.

The duty manager has a privileged override. A bay can be frozen, which stops rounds being prepared
against it and rolls back any round already heading for it, and thawed again later. The manager can
also carry a batch across by hand, moving it out of one bay and into another in one step with no
round and no vote at all.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a batch is lifted out of an open source bay into
escrow and a round is opened on an open destination; Aye and Nay, in which a party casts its single
vote; Commit, in which both votes in favour and an open destination put the batch into the
destination bay; Rollback, in which a vote against or a frozen destination puts the batch back where
it came from; Freeze and Thaw, in which the duty manager closes and reopens a bay; and Carry, in
which the duty manager moves a batch between bays by hand.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bags piled across all holding bays plus the batch sitting in the router's escrow
always equal the terminal's total.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Units, Patients, MaxVer, Free, NoLabel, NoBid

VARIABLES owner, ver, label, bid

vars == <<owner, ver, label, bid>>

Labels == [patient: Patients, ver: 0 .. MaxVer]
Bids == [unit: Units, patient: Patients, saw: 0 .. MaxVer]

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Units -> Patients \cup {Free}]
    /\ ver \in [Units -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ label \in [Units -> Labels \cup {NoLabel}]
    /\ bid \in Bids \cup {NoBid}

Init ==
    /\ owner = [u \in Units |-> Free]
    /\ ver = [u \in Units |-> 0]
    /\ label = [u \in Units |-> NoLabel]
    /\ bid = NoBid

\* Nothing is locked: the bench notes the unit's version and goes away to
\* cross-match, and the register is free to move underneath it.
Request(u, p) ==
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ bid' = [unit |-> u, patient |-> p, saw |-> ver[u]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, label>>

Allocate ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ ver[bid.unit] = bid.saw
    /\ owner[bid.unit] = Free
    /\ ver[bid.unit] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![bid.unit] = bid.patient]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![bid.unit] = @ + 1]
    /\ label' = [label EXCEPT ![bid.unit] = [patient |-> bid.patient,
                                             ver |-> ver[bid.unit] + 1]]
    /\ bid' = NoBid

Refuse ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ \/ ver[bid.unit] # bid.saw
       \/ owner[bid.unit] # Free
       \/ ver[bid.unit] = MaxVer
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, label>>

Transfuse(u) ==
    /\ owner[u] # Free
    /\ ver[u] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = Free]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![u] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, bid>>

\* Privileged override: the consultant haematologist reassigns a unit in the
\* register on the spot. The bag itself is not relabelled, so the label it is
\* carrying is now behind the register and counts for nothing.
Reassign(u, p) ==
    /\ owner[u] # Free
    /\ owner[u] # p
    /\ ver[u] < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = p]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![u] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, bid>>

Reprint(u) ==
    /\ owner[u] # Free
    /\ label' = [label EXCEPT ![u] = [patient |-> owner[u], ver |-> ver[u]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, bid>>

Strip(u) ==
    /\ label[u] # NoLabel
    /\ label' = [label EXCEPT ![u] = NoLabel]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, bid>>

Recycle(u) ==
    /\ ver[u] = MaxVer
    /\ owner[u] = Free
    /\ label[u] = NoLabel
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, label, bid>>

Settling == Allocate \/ Refuse

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Units, p \in Patients : Request(u, p) \/ Reassign(u, p)
    \/ Settling
    \/ \E u \in Units : Transfuse(u) \/ Reprint(u) \/ Strip(u) \/ Recycle(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* A label whose version still matches the register names the patient the
\* register holds that unit for, so no unit is ever carrying a live label for
\* one patient while allocated to another.
LiveLabelAgrees ==
    \A u \in Units :
        (label[u] # NoLabel /\ label[u].ver = ver[u]) => owner[u] = label[u].patient

\* The cross-match bench never sits on a request.
RequestsSettle == (bid # NoBid) ~> (bid = NoBid)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Units = {unO1, unO2}
    Patients = {ptAsh, ptBrook}
    MaxVer = 2
    Free = Free
    NoLabel = NoLabel
    NoBid = NoBid
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LiveLabelAgrees
PROPERTY RequestsSettle
nl:
A hospital blood bank allocates units of blood to patients. A unit goes to one patient and one
patient only, and the physical bag carries a printed label naming the patient it is reserved for.
The dangerous state is a bag carrying a live label for one patient while the register has it
allocated to somebody else — that is how the wrong blood reaches a bedside.

The register is versioned and the cross-match bench takes no locks. The bench notes the version a
unit is on and goes away to cross-match, leaving the register free to move underneath it. The
allocation only lands if the version is still the one it noted and the unit is still unallocated;
landing it bumps the unit's version and prints a fresh label carrying the patient and the new
version. If the version moved, or the unit was allocated in the meantime, the request is refused and
the bench starts again. One request is on the bench at a time and the bench never sits on it. When a
unit is transfused it goes back to unallocated and its version bumps again, which leaves whatever
label the bag is carrying behind the register.

The consultant haematologist has a privileged override and can reassign a unit in the register on the
spot, without going near the bag. The version bumps but the bag is not relabelled, so the label it is
carrying is behind the register and counts for nothing until somebody reprints it. Labels are
reprinted from the register when a bag is checked, and stripped off when a bag is boxed up. A unit
whose version has run to the end of its range, with nothing allocated and no label on the bag, has
its version recycled back to the start.

The full set of actions is: Request, in which the bench notes a unit's version and takes on a
cross-match for a patient; Allocate, in which the allocation lands because the version is unmoved and
the unit unallocated, bumping the version and printing a fresh label; Refuse, in which the request is
turned down; Transfuse, in which an allocated unit is used and goes back to unallocated with its
version bumped; Reassign, in which the haematologist reassigns a unit in the register without
relabelling the bag; Reprint, in which a bag's label is reprinted from the register; Strip, in which
a label is taken off a bag; and Recycle, in which an unallocated, unlabelled unit's version is reset.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any label whose version still matches the register names exactly the patient the
register has that unit allocated to, so no unit ever carries a live label for one patient while
allocated to another.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The cross-match bench never sits on a request: every one is eventually either
allocated or refused.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Boxes, MaxRev, QCap, Blank

VARIABLES rev, body, pend, frozen

vars == <<rev, body, pend, frozen>>

Amends == [by: Boxes, base: 0 .. MaxRev]

TypeOK ==
    /\ rev \in 0 .. MaxRev
    /\ body \in [1 .. MaxRev -> Amends \cup {Blank}]
    /\ Len(pend) <= QCap
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(pend) : pend[i] \in Amends
    /\ frozen \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ body = [k \in 1 .. MaxRev |-> Blank]
    /\ pend = <<>>
    /\ frozen = FALSE

\* Backpressure: the amendment queue is bounded and closed while frozen. An
\* amendment is drafted against whatever revision the book is on at the time.
Draft(b) ==
    /\ ~frozen
    /\ Len(pend) < QCap
    /\ pend' = Append(pend, [by |-> b, base |-> rev])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, body, frozen>>

\* An amendment lands only while the book is still on the revision it was
\* drafted against; anything else would write over an edit it never saw.
Apply ==
    /\ pend # <<>>
    /\ Head(pend).base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ body' = [body EXCEPT ![rev + 1] = Head(pend)]
    /\ pend' = Tail(pend)
    /\ UNCHANGED frozen

Bounce ==
    /\ pend # <<>>
    /\ \/ Head(pend).base # rev
       \/ rev = MaxRev
    /\ pend' = Tail(pend)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, body, frozen>>

\* Privileged override: the line controller writes an amendment straight into
\* the book, jumping the queue, but still against the revision it supersedes.
Force(b) ==
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ body' = [body EXCEPT ![rev + 1] = [by |-> b, base |-> rev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, frozen>>

Freeze ==
    /\ frozen' = ~frozen
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, body, pend>>

Reissue ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ pend = <<>>
    /\ rev' = 0
    /\ body' = [k \in 1 .. MaxRev |-> Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, frozen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Draft(b) \/ Force(b)
    \/ Apply \/ Bounce \/ Freeze \/ Reissue

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every revision the working book has been through was written against the
\* revision immediately before it, and none is missing, so no amendment was
\* ever laid down over one its author had not seen.
RevisionsAreContiguous ==
    \A k \in 1 .. MaxRev :
        k <= rev => (body[k] # Blank /\ body[k].base = k - 1)

====

CONSTANTS
    Boxes = {bxNorth, bxSouth}
    MaxRev = 2
    QCap = 2
    Blank = Blank
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RevisionsAreContiguous
nl:
A subway line runs off a working timetable book that every signal box amends. The book is versioned:
revision one is the first amendment ever written into it, revision two the next, and so on. The
hazard is a lost update — one box's amendment written over a revision it never saw, quietly undoing
what another box just put in.

Amendments queue on a bounded list with backpressure. A box drafts an amendment against whatever
revision the book is on at that moment, and the draft carries that base revision with it. Once the
queue is at its cap no further drafts are taken, and the queue is closed altogether while the book is
frozen.

The queue is worked from the front. An amendment lands only while the book is still on the revision
it was drafted against; landing it writes the amendment in as the next revision and moves the book
on. If the book has moved in the meantime, or the book has reached the end of its revision range,
the amendment is bounced off the queue and its box has to draft again from the revision now in force.

The line controller has a privileged override and can write an amendment straight into the book,
jumping the queue entirely. Even then the amendment goes in against the revision it supersedes, so
the book's chain of revisions stays unbroken. When the book reaches the end of its range and nothing
is queued, it is reissued and starts again from revision zero.

The full set of actions is: Draft, in which a box puts an amendment on the tail of the queue against
the revision in force, while the queue is open and below its cap; Apply, in which the amendment at
the front lands because the book is still on the revision it was drafted against, becoming the next
revision; Bounce, in which the amendment at the front is thrown off because the book has moved or
run out of range; Force, in which the line controller writes an amendment straight into the book
against the revision it supersedes; Freeze, in which the controller closes or reopens the queue; and
Reissue, in which a book at the end of its range with nothing queued starts again from zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every revision the working book has been through carries as its base the revision
immediately before it, and no revision in the chain is missing, so no amendment was ever laid down
over a revision its author had not seen.

---- MODULE W4Od19m6p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Readers, Copies, Horizon, MaxHold, Vacant, NoCharge

VARIABLES hold, clock, charged, charging, waived

vars == <<hold, clock, charged, charging, waived>>

Holds == [to: Readers, until: 1 .. Horizon]
Charges == [copy: Copies, to: Readers]

Live(c) == hold[c] # Vacant /\ hold[c].until > clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ hold \in [Copies -> Holds \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ charged \subseteq Copies
    /\ charging \in Charges \cup {NoCharge}
    /\ waived \subseteq Copies

Init ==
    /\ hold = [c \in Copies |-> Vacant]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ charged = {}
    /\ charging = NoCharge
    /\ waived = {}

\* A hold is a lease with an expiry, not a standing claim on the copy.
Reserve(r, c, len) ==
    /\ ~Live(c)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![c] = [to |-> r, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, charged, charging, waived>>

\* Raising a loss charge is one-way: the reader's account is debited and the
\* library will not take it back, so it must happen to a copy once only.
Begin(c) ==
    /\ charging = NoCharge
    /\ c \notin charged
    /\ c \notin waived
    /\ Live(c)
    /\ charging' = [copy |-> c, to |-> hold[c].to]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged, waived>>

Charge ==
    /\ charging # NoCharge
    /\ charged' = charged \cup {charging.copy}
    /\ charging' = NoCharge
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, waived>>

Drop ==
    /\ charging # NoCharge
    /\ charging' = NoCharge
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged, waived>>

\* A charge in progress rests on the hold that justifies it: the moment the
\* hold lapses or is reaped, the charge falls away with it.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ charging' = IF charging # NoCharge /\ hold[charging.copy].until <= clock + 1
                   THEN NoCharge ELSE charging
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, charged, waived>>

Reap(c) ==
    /\ hold[c] # Vacant
    /\ hold[c].until <= clock
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![c] = Vacant]
    /\ charging' = IF charging # NoCharge /\ charging.copy = c THEN NoCharge ELSE charging
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, charged, waived>>

\* Privileged override: the head librarian waives a copy, which stops a charge
\* being raised on it and knocks any charge already in progress off the desk.
Waive(c) ==
    /\ c \notin waived
    /\ waived' = waived \cup {c}
    /\ charging' = IF charging # NoCharge /\ charging.copy = c THEN NoCharge ELSE charging
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged>>

Unwaive(c) ==
    /\ c \in waived
    /\ waived' = waived \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged, charging>>

NewYear ==
    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ charging = NoCharge
    /\ \A c \in Copies : hold[c] = Vacant
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, charged, charging, waived>>

Settling == Charge \/ Drop

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Readers, c \in Copies, n \in 1 .. MaxHold : Reserve(r, c, n)
    \/ \E c \in Copies : Begin(c) \/ Reap(c) \/ Waive(c) \/ Unwaive(c)
    \/ Settling \/ Tick \/ NewYear

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* A loss charge on the desk is for a copy that has not been charged already,
\* and rests on a hold that is still live and names the very reader being
\* charged, so the one-way debit can never be raised twice on one copy.
ChargeRestsOnLiveHold ==
    charging # NoCharge =>
        /\ charging.copy \notin charged
        /\ hold[charging.copy] # Vacant
        /\ hold[charging.copy].to = charging.to
        /\ hold[charging.copy].until > clock

\* Nothing is left sitting on the charge desk.
ChargeDeskClears == (charging # NoCharge) ~> (charging = NoCharge)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Readers = {rdAsh, rdBel}
    Copies = {cpAtlas, cpPoems}
    Horizon = 3
    MaxHold = 2
    Vacant = Vacant
    NoCharge = NoCharge
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ChargeRestsOnLiveHold
PROPERTY ChargeDeskClears
nl:
A library reservation system puts holds on copies and, when a copy is not returned, raises a loss
charge against the reader who had it. Raising the charge is the one act the library will not take
back: the reader's account is debited and the debit stands. Charging the same copy twice bills a
reader for one book two or three times over, so it must happen to a copy once and once only.

Holds are leases with an expiry rather than standing claims. A copy is put on hold for a reader for
a chosen number of days, provided no live hold is already on it and the expiry falls inside the
year. Holds that have run out are reaped and the copy goes back on the shelf.

A loss charge is raised at the charge desk, one at a time. It is begun only for a copy that has not
already been charged, is not waived, and is under a live hold — the hold is what says whose account
to debit. A charge in progress rests on that hold: the moment the hold lapses as the clock moves on,
or is reaped, the charge falls off the desk with it, and the desk is never left occupied. A charge
can also simply be dropped by the assistant.

The head librarian has a privileged override and can waive a copy: no charge may be begun on it, and
any charge already on the desk for it is knocked off. A waiver can be lifted later. At the year end,
with the desk clear and no holds outstanding, the clock is reset.

The full set of actions is: Reserve, in which a copy with no live hold is put on hold for a reader,
expiring inside the year; Begin, in which a charge is taken to the desk for a copy that is unwaived,
uncharged and under a live hold; Charge, in which the debit is raised and the copy recorded as
charged; Drop, in which the assistant abandons the charge on the desk; Tick, in which the clock
advances a day and a charge whose hold has just lapsed falls off the desk; Reap, in which a hold that
has run out is cleared, taking any charge on the desk for that copy with it; Waive and Unwaive, in
which the head librarian waives a copy and lifts the waiver; and NewYear, in which the clock is reset
with the desk clear and no holds outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any loss charge on the desk is for a copy that has not been charged already and
rests on a hold that is still live and names the very reader being charged, so the one-way debit can
never be raised twice on the same copy.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The charge desk is never left occupied: a charge taken to it is always eventually
raised or cleared away.

---- MODULE W4Od19m8p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Staff, Branches, Bays, NoOne, NoCopy, Copies

Slots == Branches \X Bays
BranchOf(s) == s[1]

VARIABLES desk, ticket, pencilled, shelved

vars == <<desk, ticket, pencilled, shelved>>

Hands == Staff \cup {NoOne}

Somewhere(c) ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : shelved[s] = c
    \/ \E s \in Slots : pencilled[s] = c

TypeOK ==
    /\ desk \in [Branches -> Hands]
    /\ ticket \in [Slots -> Hands]
    /\ pencilled \in [Slots -> Copies \cup {NoCopy}]
    /\ shelved \in [Slots -> Copies \cup {NoCopy}]

Init ==
    /\ desk = [b \in Branches |-> NoOne]
    /\ ticket = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ pencilled = [s \in Slots |-> NoCopy]
    /\ shelved = [s \in Slots |-> NoCopy]

\* Coarse before fine: an assistant works one branch desk at a time and only
\* then draws the ticket for a single empty bay in that branch.
TakeDesk(p, b) ==
    /\ desk[b] = NoOne
    /\ \A k \in Branches : desk[k] # p
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![b] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticket, pencilled, shelved>>

DrawTicket(p, s) ==
    /\ desk[BranchOf(s)] = p
    /\ ticket[s] = NoOne
    /\ shelved[s] = NoCopy
    /\ \A k \in Slots : ticket[k] # p
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, pencilled, shelved>>

\* Pencilling a copy into a bay is the allocation; it is only ever done by the
\* assistant holding that bay's ticket, and only for a copy nowhere else.
Pencil(p, s, c) ==
    /\ ticket[s] = p
    /\ pencilled[s] = NoCopy
    /\ shelved[s] = NoCopy
    /\ ~Somewhere(c)
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, ticket, shelved>>

Place(p, s) ==
    /\ ticket[s] = p
    /\ pencilled[s] # NoCopy
    /\ shelved' = [shelved EXCEPT ![s] = pencilled[s]]
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![s] = NoCopy]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED desk

Rub(p, s) ==
    /\ ticket[s] = p
    /\ pencilled[s] # NoCopy
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![s] = NoCopy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, ticket, shelved>>

ReturnTicket(p, s) ==
    /\ ticket[s] = p
    /\ pencilled[s] = NoCopy
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, pencilled, shelved>>

LeaveDesk(p, b) ==
    /\ desk[b] = p
    /\ \A s \in Slots : BranchOf(s) = b => ticket[s] # p
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticket, pencilled, shelved>>

Collect(s) ==
    /\ shelved[s] # NoCopy
    /\ shelved' = [shelved EXCEPT ![s] = NoCopy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, ticket, pencilled>>

\* Privileged override: the head librarian strips a bay -- ticket, pencilling
\* and copy all at once -- without asking whoever was holding it.
Strip(s) ==
    /\ \/ ticket[s] # NoOne
       \/ pencilled[s] # NoCopy
       \/ shelved[s] # NoCopy
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![s] = NoCopy]
    /\ shelved' = [shelved EXCEPT ![s] = NoCopy]
    /\ UNCHANGED desk

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Staff, b \in Branches : TakeDesk(p, b) \/ LeaveDesk(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Staff, s \in Slots :
           DrawTicket(p, s) \/ Place(p, s) \/ Rub(p, s) \/ ReturnTicket(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Staff, s \in Slots, c \in Copies : Pencil(p, s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Collect(s) \/ Strip(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A bay with a copy pencilled into it is a bay somebody is holding the ticket
\* for and which is not already holding a copy, so a bay is never allocated to
\* two copies at once.
PencilledBaysAreHeldAndEmpty ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        pencilled[s] # NoCopy => (ticket[s] # NoOne /\ shelved[s] = NoCopy)

====
nl:
A library holds reserved books for collection on hold shelves, one bay per reserved copy. A bay takes
one copy: allocating the same bay to two copies means one reader walks off with the other's
reservation, so a bay must never be allocated twice.

Shelving is worked at two levels. An assistant takes a branch desk, working one branch at a time,
and only then draws the ticket for a single empty bay in that branch — one ticket per assistant. The
ticket is what says who is allocating that bay.

Allocation itself is done in pencil first. The assistant holding a bay's ticket pencils a copy into
it, and only a copy that is not already pencilled into or sitting in any bay anywhere. Placing the
copy turns the pencilling into a shelved copy and gives the ticket back in the same movement.
Rubbing out leaves the bay empty and the ticket still held. A ticket is given back once nothing is
pencilled against it, and a branch desk is left once the assistant holds no ticket in that branch.
Readers collect their copies off the shelf, which empties the bay.

The head librarian has a privileged override and can strip a bay outright — ticket, pencilling and
copy all at once — without asking whoever was holding it. That is how a bay is recovered when an
assistant goes home mid-task.

The full set of actions is: TakeDesk, in which an assistant working no branch takes a free branch
desk; DrawTicket, in which the assistant on a branch draws the ticket for an empty bay in it, holding
no other ticket; Pencil, in which the ticket holder pencils in a copy that is nowhere else; Place, in
which the pencilled copy is shelved and the ticket given back; Rub, in which the pencilling is rubbed
out; ReturnTicket, in which a ticket with nothing pencilled against it is given back; LeaveDesk, in
which an assistant holding no ticket in a branch leaves its desk; Collect, in which a reader takes a
copy off the shelf; and Strip, in which the head librarian clears a bay's ticket, pencilling and copy
at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bay with a copy pencilled into it is one somebody is holding the ticket for and
which is not already holding a copy, so a bay is never allocated to two copies at once.

---- MODULE W4Od2m1p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS FleetSize, Bins, TotalTotes

Bots == 0 .. FleetSize - 1
Nxt(r) == (r + 1) % FleetSize

VARIABLES bin, grip, belt, baton, alive

vars == <<bin, grip, belt, baton, alive>>

RECURSIVE Stacked(_)
Stacked(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN bin[b] + Stacked(S \ {b})

Carried == Cardinality({r \in Bots : grip[r] = 1})

TypeOK ==
    /\ bin \in [Bins -> 0 .. TotalTotes]
    /\ grip \in [Bots -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ belt \in 0 .. TotalTotes
    /\ baton \in Bots
    /\ alive \subseteq Bots

Init ==
    /\ bin = [b \in Bins |-> 0]
    /\ grip = [r \in Bots |-> 0]
    /\ belt = TotalTotes
    /\ baton = 0
    /\ alive = Bots

\* The baton walks the ring; only the live robot holding it may touch a tote.
PassBaton ==
    /\ baton \in alive
    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, alive>>

Lift(r) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 0
    /\ belt > 0
    /\ belt' = belt - 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, baton, alive>>

Stow(r, b) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ bin' = [bin EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, baton, alive>>

Recirculate(b) ==
    /\ bin[b] > 0
    /\ bin' = [bin EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ belt' = belt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grip, baton, alive>>

\* A robot can die on the spot with no word, still holding the baton and
\* whatever was in its gripper.
Die(r) ==
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ alive \ {r} # {}
    /\ alive' = alive \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, baton>>

\* The fleet supervisor puts the baton back into circulation whenever it is
\* stranded on a dead robot.
Reissue(r) ==
    /\ baton \notin alive
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ baton' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, alive>>

Salvage(r) ==
    /\ r \notin alive
    /\ grip[r] = 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ belt' = belt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, baton, alive>>

Revive(r) ==
    /\ r \notin alive
    /\ grip[r] = 0
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, baton>>

Reissuing == \E r \in Bots : Reissue(r)

Next ==
    \/ PassBaton
    \/ \E r \in Bots : Lift(r) \/ Die(r) \/ Salvage(r) \/ Revive(r)
    \/ \E r \in Bots, b \in Bins : Stow(r, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bins : Recirculate(b)
    \/ Reissuing

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Reissuing)

\* Totes only ever move between the belt, a gripper and a bin, so the totes
\* stacked in bins plus those in grippers plus those on the belt always come to
\* the fleet total -- a robot dying mid-carry loses nothing.
TotesConserved == Stacked(Bins) + Carried + belt = TotalTotes

\* The baton never stays stranded on a dead robot.
BatonComesBack == (baton \notin alive) ~> (baton \in alive)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    FleetSize = 3
    Bins = {bnPick, bnPack}
    TotalTotes = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TotesConserved
PROPERTY BatonComesBack
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet works a recirculating belt of totes. The floor starts with a fixed number of
totes and the robots only ever move them between the belt, their own grippers and the stacking bins;
nothing is added and nothing is lost. So the totes stacked in the bins, plus those in grippers, plus
those on the belt, must always come to the floor total — including when a robot dies in the middle of
a carry.

Only one robot works at a time, and the right to work travels with a baton that walks the fleet ring
one robot at a time. The robot holding the baton, and only that robot, may lift a tote off the belt
into its gripper, or stow the tote it is carrying into a bin. Totes are put back onto the belt from
the bins as the picking rounds come round again.

A robot can die on the spot with no word at all — no fault code, no handover — still holding the
baton and whatever was in its gripper. Nothing it holds is released by the death itself. The fleet
supervisor puts the baton back into circulation whenever it is stranded on a dead robot, and the
baton never stays stranded. A tote left in a dead robot's gripper is salvaged back onto the belt,
and a robot with an empty gripper can be revived and rejoin the ring. At least one robot is always
left running.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which a live baton holder passes it to the next robot round
the ring; Lift, in which the live baton holder takes a tote off the belt into its empty gripper;
Stow, in which the live baton holder puts the tote it carries into a bin; Recirculate, in which a
tote goes from a bin back onto the belt; Die, in which a robot stops dead while still holding the
baton and its tote, provided at least one other robot is left running; Reissue, in which the
supervisor puts a stranded baton back onto a live robot; Salvage, in which a tote is recovered from a
dead robot's gripper back onto the belt; and Revive, in which a dead robot with an empty gripper
rejoins the fleet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The totes stacked across the bins plus those held in robot grippers plus those on
the belt always equal the floor total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The baton never stays stranded on a dead robot — it is always eventually put back
onto a live one.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Flights, Slots, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES allocs, cfg, closed, held

vars == <<allocs, cfg, closed, held>>

Allocations == [slot: Slots, flight: Flights, epoch: 0 .. MaxEpoch]

Current == {a \in allocs : a.epoch = cfg}
SlotTaken(s) == \E a \in Current : a.slot = s
FlightBooked(f) == \E a \in Current : a.flight = f

TypeOK ==
    /\ allocs \subseteq Allocations
    /\ cfg \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ closed \subseteq Slots
    /\ held \subseteq Flights

Init ==
    /\ allocs = {}
    /\ cfg = 0
    /\ closed = {}
    /\ held = {}

\* Every allocation is stamped with the runway configuration it was made
\* under; only allocations stamped with the running configuration count.
Allocate(s, f) ==
    /\ s \notin closed
    /\ f \notin held
    /\ ~SlotTaken(s)
    /\ ~FlightBooked(f)
    /\ allocs' = allocs \cup {[slot |-> s, flight |-> f, epoch |-> cfg]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cfg, closed, held>>

Release(a) ==
    /\ a \in allocs
    /\ allocs' = allocs \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cfg, closed, held>>

Purge(a) ==
    /\ a \in allocs
    /\ a.epoch # cfg
    /\ allocs' = allocs \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cfg, closed, held>>

\* Reconfiguring the runway direction renumbers the configuration, which puts
\* every allocation made under the old one behind.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ cfg < MaxEpoch
    /\ cfg' = cfg + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, closed, held>>

Restart ==
    /\ cfg = MaxEpoch
    /\ allocs = {}
    /\ cfg' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, closed, held>>

\* Privileged override: the watch supervisor bumps a flight straight into a
\* slot, clearing whatever current allocation was on it first.
Bump(s, f) ==
    /\ f \notin held
    /\ ~FlightBooked(f)
    /\ allocs' = {a \in allocs : ~(a.epoch = cfg /\ a.slot = s)}
                     \cup {[slot |-> s, flight |-> f, epoch |-> cfg]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cfg, closed, held>>

Close(s) ==
    /\ s \notin closed
    /\ closed' = closed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, cfg, held>>

Reopen(s) ==
    /\ s \in closed
    /\ closed' = closed \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, cfg, held>>

Hold(f) ==
    /\ f \notin held
    /\ ~FlightBooked(f)
    /\ held' = held \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, cfg, closed>>

Unhold(f) ==
    /\ f \in held
    /\ held' = held \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocs, cfg, closed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, f \in Flights : Allocate(s, f) \/ Bump(s, f)
    \/ \E a \in allocs : Release(a) \/ Purge(a)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Close(s) \/ Reopen(s)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Hold(f) \/ Unhold(f)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Restart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Among the allocations stamped with the running configuration, the slot
\* determines the flight, so no departure slot is ever allocated to two
\* flights under the configuration actually in force.
SlotAllocatedOnce ==
    \A a, b \in Current : a.slot = b.slot => a.flight = b.flight

====
nl:
An airport allocates departure slots on its runway. A slot goes to one flight: two aircraft holding
the same departure window means two rolling for one gap in the arrivals stream.

The runway is run under a numbered configuration — which direction it is operating in, which taxiways
are live. Every allocation is stamped with the configuration it was made under, and only allocations
stamped with the configuration currently in force count for anything. An allocation from an earlier
configuration describes a runway that is not the one out of the window, so it binds nothing; it is
simply purged when anybody gets round to it.

A slot is allocated to a flight only if that slot is open, is not already allocated under the running
configuration, the flight is not already holding a slot under it, and the flight is not in the
holding stack. Allocations are released when the flight departs or the plan changes. Reconfiguring
the runway renumbers the configuration, which puts every allocation made under the old one behind at
a stroke; once the register is empty at the end of the range the numbering starts again.

The watch supervisor has a privileged override. A flight can be bumped straight into a slot, and
whatever current allocation that slot was carrying is cleared out in the same movement, so the
override never leaves two flights on one slot. The supervisor can also close a slot to new
allocations and reopen it, and can put a flight into the holding stack or take it out.

The full set of actions is: Allocate, in which an open, unallocated slot is given to a flight that
holds nothing and is not in the stack, stamped with the running configuration; Release, in which an
allocation is given up; Purge, in which an allocation stamped with an earlier configuration is
cleared away; Reconfigure, in which the configuration is renumbered; Restart, in which the numbering
goes back to the start with the register empty; Bump, in which the supervisor puts a flight into a
slot, clearing that slot's current allocation first; Close and Reopen, in which a slot is taken out
of and put back into use; and Hold and Unhold, in which a flight is put into and taken out of the
holding stack.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Among the allocations stamped with the configuration actually in force, the slot
determines the flight, so no departure slot is ever allocated to two flights at once.

---- MODULE W4Od19m0p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Branches, MaxRev, MaxShelf, NoBid

VARIABLES rev, queued, sawRev, sawLen, shelf, bid

vars == <<rev, queued, sawRev, sawLen, shelf, bid>>

Bids == [by: Branches, base: 0 .. MaxRev, want: {"join", "leave"}]

TypeOK ==
    /\ rev \in 0 .. MaxRev
    /\ queued \in 0 .. MaxShelf
    /\ sawRev \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ sawLen \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxShelf]
    /\ shelf \in 1 .. MaxShelf
    /\ bid \in Bids \cup {NoBid}

Init ==
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ queued = 0
    /\ sawRev = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ sawLen = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ shelf = MaxShelf
    /\ bid = NoBid

Refresh(b) ==
    /\ sawRev' = [sawRev EXCEPT ![b] = rev]
    /\ sawLen' = [sawLen EXCEPT ![b] = queued]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queued, shelf, bid>>

\* No lock is taken: the branch works from the copy it last read and stamps
\* its request with the revision that copy came from.
Propose(b, w) ==
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ bid' = [by |-> b, base |-> sawRev[b], want |-> w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queued, sawRev, sawLen, shelf>>

\* A request lands only if the queue record is still on the revision it was
\* worked out from; landing it rolls the revision on.
Accept ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ bid.base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ IF bid.want = "join" THEN queued < shelf ELSE queued > 0
    /\ queued' = IF bid.want = "join" THEN queued + 1 ELSE queued - 1
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sawRev, sawLen, shelf>>

Decline ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ \/ bid.base # rev
       \/ rev = MaxRev
       \/ (bid.want = "join" /\ queued >= shelf)
       \/ (bid.want = "leave" /\ queued = 0)
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queued, sawRev, sawLen, shelf>>

\* The hold shelf is resized while the service runs, never below what is
\* already sitting on it.
Resize(n) ==
    /\ n >= queued
    /\ shelf' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queued, sawRev, sawLen, bid>>

\* Reissuing the catalogue restarts the numbering and re-syncs every branch in
\* the same movement, so no branch is left holding a number that has come round.
Reissue ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ rev' = 0
    /\ sawRev' = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ sawLen' = [b \in Branches |-> queued]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, shelf, bid>>

Settling == Accept \/ Decline

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Refresh(b)
    \/ \E b \in Branches, w \in {"join", "leave"} : Propose(b, w)
    \/ Settling
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxShelf : Resize(n)
    \/ Reissue

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* Any branch whose copy carries the revision the record is actually on is
\* holding the queue length the record actually has, so no branch's update was
\* ever written over one it had not read.
CopiesAgreeAtRevision ==
    \A b \in Branches : sawRev[b] = rev => sawLen[b] = queued

\* The reservations desk never sits on a request.
BidsSettle == (bid # NoBid) ~> (bid = NoBid)

====

CONSTANTS
    Branches = {brCentral, brRiverside}
    MaxRev = 2
    MaxShelf = 2
    NoBid = NoBid
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CopiesAgreeAtRevision
PROPERTY BidsSettle
nl:
A library group keeps one reservation queue per title, shared across its branches. The queue record
holds how many readers are waiting and carries a revision number that rolls on every time the record
changes. The hazard is a lost update: a branch writing a change it worked out from a copy of the
record that has since been replaced, silently undoing what another branch just did.

Branches take no lock. Each keeps its own copy of the queue length together with the revision that
copy came from, and refreshes it from the record whenever it likes. When a branch wants to put a
reader on the queue or take one off, it lodges a request stamped with the revision its copy came
from. One request is on the desk at a time and the desk never sits on one.

The request lands only if the record is still on the revision the branch worked from; landing it
changes the queue length and rolls the revision on. If the revision has moved in the meantime, or
the change does not fit — nobody to take off an empty queue, no room on the shelf for another — the
request is declined and the branch refreshes and starts again.

Hold shelf capacity changes while the service runs: shelves are added for the summer reading scheme
and taken away when the building work starts. The shelf is never resized below what is already
sitting on it. When the record reaches the end of its revision range the catalogue is reissued: the
numbering restarts and every branch's copy is re-synced in the same movement, so no branch is left
holding a revision number that has come round again.

The full set of actions is: Refresh, in which a branch takes a fresh copy of the queue length and
revision; Propose, in which a branch lodges a join or leave request stamped with its copy's revision;
Accept, in which the request lands because the record is still on that revision and the change fits,
rolling the revision on; Decline, in which the request is turned down; Resize, in which the hold
shelf capacity is changed at runtime, never below what is on it; and Reissue, in which the revision
numbering restarts and every branch is re-synced.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any branch whose copy carries the revision the record is actually on is holding
exactly the queue length the record actually has, so no branch's update was ever written over one it
had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The reservations desk never sits on a request: every one lodged is eventually
either accepted or declined.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Classes, NorthId, SouthId, CapNorth, CapSouth, TotalTrains

Describers == {NorthId, SouthId}

VARIABLES berths, north, south, isolated

vars == <<berths, north, south, isolated>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ berths \in 0 .. TotalTrains
    /\ Len(north) <= CapNorth
    /\ Len(south) <= CapSouth
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(north) : north[i] \in Classes
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(south) : south[i] \in Classes
    /\ isolated \subseteq Describers

Init ==
    /\ berths = TotalTrains
    /\ north = <<>>
    /\ south = <<>>
    /\ isolated = {}

\* Backpressure: a describer stops lifting descriptions once its own step
\* queue is full, and the two queues have different depths.
LiftNorth(k) ==
    /\ NorthId \notin isolated
    /\ berths > 0
    /\ Len(north) < CapNorth
    /\ berths' = berths - 1
    /\ north' = Append(north, k)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<south, isolated>>

LiftSouth(k) ==
    /\ SouthId \notin isolated
    /\ berths > 0
    /\ Len(south) < CapSouth
    /\ berths' = berths - 1
    /\ south' = Append(south, k)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<north, isolated>>

DropNorth ==
    /\ north # <<>>
    /\ berths' = berths + 1
    /\ north' = Tail(north)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<south, isolated>>

DropSouth ==
    /\ south # <<>>
    /\ berths' = berths + 1
    /\ south' = Tail(south)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<north, isolated>>

\* At the boundary a description is handed straight from one describer's queue
\* to the other's; it never touches a berth on the way.
HandNorthToSouth ==
    /\ north # <<>>
    /\ Len(south) < CapSouth
    /\ south' = Append(south, Head(north))
    /\ north' = Tail(north)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, isolated>>

HandSouthToNorth ==
    /\ south # <<>>
    /\ Len(north) < CapNorth
    /\ north' = Append(north, Head(south))
    /\ south' = Tail(south)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, isolated>>

Isolate(d) ==
    /\ d \notin isolated
    /\ isolated' = isolated \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, north, south>>

Restore(d) ==
    /\ d \in isolated
    /\ isolated' = isolated \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, north, south>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Classes : LiftNorth(k) \/ LiftSouth(k)
    \/ DropNorth \/ DropSouth
    \/ HandNorthToSouth \/ HandSouthToNorth
    \/ \E d \in Describers : Isolate(d) \/ Restore(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every train description is in exactly one place -- on a berth or in one of
\* the two describers' step queues -- so the three counts always add up to the
\* number of trains the line is describing.
DescriptionsConserved ==

CONSTANTS
    Classes = {clStopper, clExpress}
    NorthId = NorthId
    SouthId = SouthId
    CapNorth = 3
    CapSouth = 2
    TotalTrains = 4
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DescriptionsConserved
nl:
A subway line shows where its trains are on a berth display: one berth per track section, each
holding one train description. Two train describer systems drive the same display — the north
describer and the south describer, procured separately and never integrated — and they share the
one pool of berths between them.

A description that is being stepped from one berth to the next is lifted off the display into the
describer's own step queue and put back down when the step completes. Every description is therefore
in exactly one place at any instant: on a berth, or in the north describer's queue, or in the
south's. The count must always come to the number of trains the line is describing; a description
that goes missing is a train nobody can see, and one that appears twice is a phantom that will stop
a real train.

The step queues are bounded and apply backpressure, and the two are not the same depth: the north
describer has the deeper queue. A describer stops lifting descriptions off the display once its own
queue is full. At the boundary between the two systems a description is handed straight from the
head of one queue to the tail of the other, subject to the receiving queue's cap; it never touches a
berth on the way across.

Either describer can be isolated for maintenance, after which it lifts nothing new, though whatever
is already in its queue still drops back onto the display or hands across. An isolated describer is
restored when the work is done.

The full set of actions is: LiftNorth and LiftSouth, in which the describer concerned takes a
description off a berth into the tail of its own queue, while it is not isolated and its queue is
below its cap; DropNorth and DropSouth, in which the description at the head of a queue is put back
onto a berth; HandNorthToSouth and HandSouthToNorth, in which the description at the head of one
queue moves to the tail of the other, subject to that queue's cap; and Isolate and Restore, in which
a describer is taken out of service and put back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The descriptions shown on berths plus those in the north describer's queue plus
those in the south describer's queue always add up to exactly the number of trains being described.

---- MODULE W4Od15m0p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Firms, Books, TotalLots, MaxDepth, MaxVer, NoDraft

VARIABLES book, ver, pot, depth, draft

vars == <<book, ver, pot, depth, draft>>

Drafts == [firm: Firms, bk: Books, saw: 0 .. MaxVer, qty: 1 .. TotalLots]

RECURSIVE Resting(_)
Resting(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN book[b] + Resting(S \ {b})

Sound(d) ==
    /\ d # NoDraft
    /\ ver[d.bk] = d.saw
    /\ ver[d.bk] < MaxVer
    /\ book[d.bk] + d.qty <= depth[d.bk]
    /\ pot >= d.qty

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Books -> 0 .. TotalLots]
    /\ ver \in [Books -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ pot \in 0 .. TotalLots
    /\ depth \in [Books -> 1 .. MaxDepth]
    /\ draft \in Drafts \cup {NoDraft}

Init ==
    /\ book = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ ver = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ pot = TotalLots
    /\ depth = [b \in Books |-> MaxDepth]
    /\ draft = NoDraft

\* No lock: the firm reads the book's depth marker and version and works its
\* order up while the book stays open to everybody else.
Read(f, b, q) ==
    /\ draft = NoDraft
    /\ draft' = [firm |-> f, bk |-> b, saw |-> ver[b], qty |-> q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, depth>>

\* Lots move out of the pre-auction pot and into the book in one step, so
\* nothing is ever counted in both places or in neither.
Post ==
    /\ Sound(draft)
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![draft.bk] = @ + draft.qty]
    /\ pot' = pot - draft.qty
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![draft.bk] = @ + 1]
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED depth

Miss ==
    /\ draft # NoDraft
    /\ ~Sound(draft)
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, depth>>

Pull(b, q) ==
    /\ q <= book[b]
    /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![b] = @ - q]
    /\ pot' = pot + q
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depth, draft>>

\* The exchange retunes book depth between rounds while the auction runs,
\* never below what is already resting.
Retune(b, n) ==
    /\ n >= book[b]
    /\ depth' = [depth EXCEPT ![b] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, draft>>

Renumber(b) ==
    /\ ver[b] = MaxVer
    /\ draft = NoDraft
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, pot, depth, draft>>

Settling == Post \/ Miss

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Firms, b \in Books, q \in 1 .. TotalLots : Read(f, b, q)
    \/ Settling
    \/ \E b \in Books, q \in 1 .. TotalLots : Pull(b, q)
    \/ \E b \in Books, n \in 1 .. MaxDepth : Retune(b, n)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Renumber(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* Lots only ever move between the pre-auction pot and an order book, so the
\* lots resting across the books plus those still in the pot always come to
\* the session total.
LotsConserved == Resting(Books) + pot = TotalLots

\* The order desk never sits on a working order.
DraftsSettle == (draft # NoDraft) ~> (draft = NoDraft)

CONSTANTS
    Firms = {fmAlder, fmBirch}
    Books = {bkTelco, bkMiner}
    TotalLots = 2
    MaxDepth = 2
    MaxVer = 2
    NoDraft = NoDraft
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LotsConserved
PROPERTY DraftsSettle
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction with a fixed number of share lots. Lots sit either in the
pre-auction pot or resting in one of the order books, and the auction only moves them between the
two; nothing is created and nothing destroyed, so the lots resting across the books plus the lots
still in the pot must always come to the session total.

Member firms take no lock on a book. A firm reads the book's depth and its version number and works
its order up while the book stays open to everybody else. Posting the order only goes through if the
version is still the one the firm read, the book has depth left for the quantity, the pot still has
the lots, and the book's version counter has not run to the end of its range. Posting moves the lots
out of the pot and into the book in one step and rolls the book's version on. If any of those checks
fails, the order is missed and the firm works up a fresh one. One working order is on the desk at a
time and the desk never sits on it. Lots are pulled back out of a book into the pot as orders are
cancelled, which also rolls that book's version on.

Book depth is retuned while the auction runs — the exchange widens a book when interest builds and
narrows it when it thins — but never below what is already resting in it. A book whose version
counter has reached the end of its range is renumbered back to the start, with nothing on the desk,
so a stale read cannot be mistaken for a current one.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a firm takes the current version and depth of a book and
puts a working order on the empty desk; Post, in which the order goes through because the version is
unmoved, the book has room, the pot has the lots and the version range is not exhausted, moving the
lots and rolling the version on; Miss, in which the order is dropped because one of those checks
failed; Pull, in which lots are taken back out of a book into the pot and the version rolls on;
Retune, in which a book's depth is changed at runtime, never below what is resting in it; and
Renumber, in which an exhausted version counter is reset with the desk clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots resting across all the order books plus the lots still in the pre-auction
pot always equal the session total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The order desk never sits on a working order: every one is eventually either
posted or missed.
